title: Version 12: canvas-first composition, material and dark appearance, and nine defects found by rendering the product
body:
## What this is

ARQ Liquid Glass 12.0 and, continuing on the same branch, ARQ Pixel-Perfect Implementation System 13.0 — carried against the real repository rather than as a parallel shell. No new application shell, design-token system, command bus, selection store, project-state store, icon registry, `.arq` persistence path, recovery system, language system, evidence system, plan renderer or 3D renderer was created.

**Delivery stop: pull request plus verified preview. Not merge, not production.** This PR is a draft and must not be merged or deployed without separate explicit authorisation.

Per-slice detail: [`ARQ_V13_IMPLEMENTATION_LEDGER.md`](ARQ_V13_IMPLEMENTATION_LEDGER.md) and [`ARQ_V12_IMPLEMENTATION_LEDGER.md`](ARQ_V12_IMPLEMENTATION_LEDGER.md). Neither decides anything: ZEUS routes the work, Engineering OS remains merge authority.

## The dominant finding

The single most common defect in this repository is **capability built, tested, and never called**. Every item below had passing tests the whole time and no production caller:

| Module | What was missing |
|---|---|
| `roomsOnLevel` | rooms were never drawn |
| `wallOutline` | used by 3D, never by plan — walls had no thickness |
| `wallDimensions` | accepted by both surfaces, supplied by neither |
| `acquireSingleWriterLock` | two tabs could each believe they were the writer |
| `applyDefensiveOpenPolicy` | `PRAGMA foreign_keys` stayed off in the browser |
| `publishProjectFile` | a fully verified portable-copy path with no way to reach it |
| `buildArqfsRecoveryReport` / `resolveArqfsSafeModePlan` | no caller at all |
| `generateWallOpeningMeshes` | 3D had no openings |
| `roomLabelText` | two-line labels existed; the app built its own one-line version |
| `buildPlanViewport` / `exportSheetToPdf` | the product could draw a plan and not make a sheet of it |
| `mitre-join` / `butt-join` / `t-join` / `cross-join` | **still unwired** — next slice |

## What the product does now that it did not

- **Semantic plan from canonical data.** The golden fixture's ground floor draws as a plan: 37 poché-filled walls, tinted and labelled rooms, and its doors and windows as real openings — piers, jambs, leaves, swing arcs, glazing. An opening is a hole, not a lid: the wall is drawn as the stretches that remain solid, so it cannot print solid over its own doors.
- **Opening-aware 3D.** The same canonical openings cut through the extruded model. One derivation feeds both surfaces, because two would let plan and model disagree about where an opening is.
- **Vector sheet export.** `Export sheet as PDF` at 1:100 on A1. Scale is honoured rather than fitted to page — a drawing issued at 1:100 must measure 1:100 under a rule.
- **Portable publication.** `Save a copy`, verified by a fresh independent reader before any bytes are handed over, with all twelve refusal reasons given distinct, truthful copy.
- **Condition-aware open.** A working copy whose last write never committed opens read-only and says so, instead of committing on top of a revision the project never reached.
- **Designed dark appearance and a bounded material layer,** under ADR-0031 and ADR-0032.

## Demo content removed

The V13 package explicitly rejects `Untitled project`, `demo fixture`, `Fixture wall N`, and hard-coded rectangular demo models. All are gone: the 5,000 synthetic tree rows, the hard-coded 4.20 × 3.60 room in plan, the 3D starting-room outline, the two invented tree nodes, and a Delete action that journalled a note instead of deleting.

## Responsive evidence — measured, not asserted

`scripts/run-responsive-capture.mjs` captures the running product at each class in a real browser laid out at that size, with the pointer type that band really has, opening the golden fixture through the real dialog. Nothing is scaled, reused between sizes, or shown in a device frame.

| Viewport | Band the product resolved | Canvas | Fixture opens | Overflow |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1600×1000 | `desktop` | 1461×819 | yes | none |
| 1366×1024 | `desktop` | 1253×876 | yes | none |
| 1024×768 | `tablet-landscape` | 1024×577 | yes | none |
| 430×932 | `phone` | 430×767 | yes | none |

Each asserts in-page: no `demo fixture` string, no `Fixture wall` string, no horizontal overflow. A 1366px iPad landing on `desktop` is an open threshold decision for the owner, recorded rather than silently moved.

Every canvas above is wider than an earlier revision of this table recorded, and none of it came from a layout change: the browser's default `body { margin: 8px }` had never been reset, so the shell was inset 8px on every side of every band.

## Defects found and fixed

Most were invisible to the test suite and only surfaced by driving the running application: no `font-family` anywhere (the product rendered in the browser's default serif); dark mode never applied a background at the root (a full-height white rectangle where the drawing is); the viewport probe measured once at mount and read `window.innerWidth`, so a phone rendered the tablet layout; the plan opened at ~1% zoom; the Inspector described one wall as the whole selection; the phone had two competing bottom owners; rooms read `0.0 m2` because an already-square-metre value was divided by a million.

Three I caused and repaired in the same runs, each caught by a browser check rather than by tests or typecheck:

- Removing the 3D demo room left an empty scene with no bounding sphere → NaN radius → `fitBoundingSphere` threw during render and the 3D canvas never mounted.
- A *value* import from the `@arq/arqfs` barrel dragged `node:fs` into the browser bundle and failed the build.
- The capture harness waited for a string only the desktop panel renders, and nearly published "the fixture did not open" as a phone and iPad product failure.

### Correction pass: twelve more, found by reading the captures

Each verified against the running product after the fix. Full table and reasoning in the V13 ledger.

- **Room labels drawn through the walls and door swings on top of them.** The fit test compared bounding boxes, which is only right for a room that is a centred rectangle — and a label is drawn at the *centroid*. Worse, containment in a room's own ring cannot see an interior wall crossing a room whose boundary predates it (the fixture's "Linen" has exactly that), or a door swing, which sweeps into a room by design and belongs to no boundary at all. Walls and openings are now built before labels and handed over as clearance, and a label is offered the room's centre first and then positions further out rather than one position and nothing else.
- **The page inset 8px on every side of every band**, cutting sync state off the bottom of a 1024px window and taking 16px of width from a 430px phone.
- **The status strip reporting a cursor a touch device has not got**, and repeating save and sync from the bar directly above it. It keys on the pointer now, and the phone's separate tool chip — a third stacked strip above the dock — joins it.
- **An empty 38px context bar** across the bottom of the drawing, because "there is an active tool" was true on arrival with no actions to put in it.
- **The view identity pill printed over a room** wherever the drawing was fitted to fill.
- **The 3D ground plane swamping the building.** A fixed 30m square centred on the world origin, never re-placed; the fixture is a 12m house whose corner is at the origin, so it stood in one quadrant of a plane that filled the frame.
- **The Project overview rendering behind the project browser**, project name cut in half — and printing `view.kind` as copy, so its first card read "3D 3d" and "Level 1 Plan plan". `RecentViewSummary.kind` was typed `string`; it is the registry union now.
- **Two panel disclosures, one shouting in caps** like the section headings it is not, and the panel's one command drawn without an edge.

## Refused, with reasons

- **V13's `command-machine.ts`** — would be the third command state machine in a repo that already has one too many. The choice between the existing two is an open owner decision.
- **The merged "Local current" chip.** The reference composition merges save state and sync state into one green chip. `top-bar.tsx` carries the opposite as an invariant, and this build depends on it: sync is `not-configured` because no sync backend exists, while save is real and journalled. A single green chip tells a user their work is somewhere other than this device. It is not.

**One earlier refusal was reversed on owner feedback.** Tabler 3.45.0 is now the single pinned icon family, replacing the hand-drawn glyphs, and the eight-glyph house adapter is the thing it replaced rather than a second family beside it.

## Evidence

Local and uncached: **3,653 tests across 337 files**; `pnpm typecheck` (37 packages); `lint`; `format:check`; `check:editor-dependency-boundaries`; `check:dependency-licences`; `zeus-guard-test`; the Arq Language System ladder through `arq:language:audit:ci`; and all headless-Chromium capability checks.

The PDF export was driven end to end against the golden fixture: 9,775 bytes, `%PDF-` header, **2,200 vector path operators and no image XObject, DCTDecode or JPXDecode** — the vector claim is measured, not asserted.

The V13 package's own provenance checks out: ZIP SHA-256 matches the value supplied with it, and its golden fixture is byte-identical to the one already in `fixtures/`.

## Blockers — both owner actions, neither clearable by implementation

1. **GitHub Actions has produced no run for this pull request**, across every push including the most recent. The only check run against the head commit is `Vercel Preview Comments`, for the marketing site. All eight workflows report `state: active`; the pattern points at repository-level run approval or billing.
2. **No preview exists for `apps/web`.** Vercel builds `arq-website` — the marketing site — and nothing else. The delivery stop asks for a verified preview against the exact PR head, and for the code this change touches there is no preview to verify.

Because of (1), every claim above is local evidence, not a green pipeline. **No slice is marked `verified` on the pipeline's account**, and no visual baseline yet compares output against the Version 13 reference.

## Known remaining work

Wall joins (four join modules still unwired, so wall ends meet rather than mitre); tools without glyphs; the contextual Inspector and its pin concept; the recovery comparison surface; sheet sets, title blocks and page settings; the fixture's five linear dimensions, still reported as unsupported. The sheet reads as a page in light appearance and only faintly in dark, where `--arq-ui-paper` sits seven levels off `--arq-ui-canvas` — an appearance-token decision left to the owner rather than moved here.

title: Zeus 5: full prompt visibility, delegated-prompt lint, and the senior company role layer
body:
## Problem

Zeus 5 routed every prompt but showed only its compact contract, so the operator never saw the actual instructions the executor works from, delegated prompts to subagents had no enforced shape, and there was no senior role layer (CEO/CTO/engineering leads) fronting the Zeus owner roles.

## Solution

- The `UserPromptSubmit` hook now echoes, after the compact contract, the **full execution prompt** the contract compiles into: owner role, routed modules, method stack with effects, execution steps, check ladder, acceptance criteria, repair budget, handoff states, and always-on standing orders (including "any prompt written for a subagent is shown in full before dispatch"). New CLI: `node scripts/zeus.mjs prompt --task "..."` (`--with-contract`, `--format json`). `ZEUS_HOOK_PROMPT=0` reduces the echo to the compact contract alone.
- New `node scripts/zeus.mjs prompt-lint`: lints a delegated handoff prompt for the seven parts `/zeus-handoff` defines (role, context, task, acceptance, verification, critique, handoff), warns on missing non-goals, missing typed-evidence language, thin inlined context, and unmentioned authority gates. The generated execution prompt passes its own lint.
- New `company/` layer: fourteen senior roles (CEO, CTO, Chief of Staff, VP Engineering, Backend/Frontend/Geometry-BIM/AI/Security/QA leads, Product Manager, Design Lead, Marketing & Comms, Incident Commander) as context packs bound to `.zeus/role-registry.json` owner roles and the existing reviewer agents (`company/ROSTER.md`, `company/ZEUS-BRIDGE.md`). `node scripts/zeus.mjs roles --task "..."` now prints the company face per role; the new `/zeus-team` command runs one task through the whole chain autonomously. Patterns ported from the bookphysio CLEO system and adapted to Arq's contracts.

## Non-goals

- No change to classification, routing, tiers, budgets, guards, or the merge authority: roles and prompt visibility add transparency and a named owner, never authority. Engineering OS 5.0 still owns the gate and the Language System still owns wording.
- No new subagent registrations; company roles are context packs, not `.claude/agents` entries.

## Visual evidence

Not a UI change. Hook output sample (per actionable prompt): compact contract heading followed by `# Zeus 5 Execution Prompt` with the full instruction block.

## Tests

All local, all green: `bash scripts/test-zeus-system.sh` (verify, hook tests incl. two new assertions for the execution-prompt echo and the `ZEUS_HOOK_PROMPT=0` opt-out, validation, classification, guard tests, architecture lint), `pnpm arq:language:verify`, `pnpm arq:language:audit:ci`, `pnpm check:secrets`, `pnpm check:workspace-registries`, prettier and eslint on changed scripts, and `zeus prompt | zeus prompt-lint` round-trip.

## Performance effect

The hook now renders one extra markdown block per actionable prompt from the already-compiled contract; compile stays in the microsecond range (precompiled matchers unchanged).

## Accessibility effect

None (internal tooling and markdown docs only).

## Project format and migration effect

None. No `.arq`, schema or persistence surface touched.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No dependencies added or changed; new scripts use `node:fs` only.

## Security and privacy effect

No new secret handling or network access. The delegated-prompt standing order plus `prompt-lint` reduce the risk of dispatching under-specified or unseen prompts; the deterministic guards are untouched and still pinned by `zeus-guard-test.mjs` (23 cases green).

## Rollback

Revert the single commit `1470f7e`; `ZEUS_HOOK_PROMPT=0` also disables the new hook output without a revert. New files (`company/`, `zeus-prompt*.mjs`, `/zeus-team`) are additive and safe to delete.

title: Implement the ARQ CAD Pack 3.0 backlog: lifecycle, operations, units, references, constraints, inference
body:
## Problem

The ARQ CAD System Implementation Pack 3.0 carries a 205-task backlog (`machine/backlog-v3.csv`), every row `state: proposed`. Much of P1–P3 was already merged at HEAD; the phases that gate everything downstream were not implemented.

## Solution

Forty commits across P1–P13. **`docs/product/V3-IMPLEMENTATION-TRACEABILITY.csv` maps all 205 tasks** to where each was addressed or why it was not — read that first, it is the only way to check this PR's claims task by task.

| Disposition | Count |
| --- | --- |
| Implemented on this branch | 119 |
| Pre-existing (verified, not assumed) | 49 |
| Owner-authority (P0 checks, P14 release, workflow pinning, build provenance) | 28 |
| Implemented differently (V3-032, V3-035, V3-039, V3-142, V3-143, V3-148) | 6 |
| Blocked for want of evidence (V3-107, V3-108, V3-117) | 3 |

The record is generated and every row verified: each names an evidence path and a symbol that must appear in it, and the generator fails rather than writing a claim the repository cannot support. It failed once while being written — a job in `security.yml` rather than `ci.yml`.

### Publication and recovery (P5)

The flow reached `published` directly from `publishing` on a bare event, while its own copy told the user *"The published file was reopened and checked"*. Nothing performed that check — the reassurance was the fabricated part. `publishProjectFile` reopens published bytes through a reader sharing no page cache, statement cache or transaction with the writer, and requires that reader's own findings to match on identity, revision and semantic hash. A dropped-entry test proves the point: SQLite still considers that file sound.

`RecoveryPlan.autoApply` is the literal type `false`, so no caller can build a plan that authorises its own application. A journal built on a revision *newer* than the working copy is refused whole, since replaying the matching subset would commit a partial history.

**Publication is now reachable from the browser.** It runs as a Worker command, because `VACUUM INTO` writes through the VFS and only the Worker holds the `opfs-sahpool` utility that can reopen the result as an independent connection — a main thread handed the bytes and asked to verify them would be checking a copy of a copy, which is the property publication depends on, broken. The bytes and the verdict travel on one response, so no caller can hand a file to a user without the receipt saying it was checked; a verified publication that returns no bytes is reported as a refusal, because a success with no file is the one outcome that must not be called success. `NativeProjectSession.publish` queues behind in-flight saves rather than racing them into a `working-copy-not-settled` refusal.

### Typed operations (P4)

One commit path: refuse read-only, reject a stale base revision, check preconditions against current state, apply, validate the *candidate*, commit in one transaction, read the revision back rather than incrementing locally. Every rejection returns the caller's original state and revision, asserted across all six rejection paths.

### Canonical units (P8)

The spike measures rather than argues, and **contradicts the pack's own reasoning**: `bigint` is 13.6× slower, while integer micrometres in a `number` are about twice as fast as float64. The assumed cost of the decision is not a cost. What it confirms is why it matters — float64 fails route-independent equality (300mm reached two ways are different floats), which is what makes a semantic hash unusable as proof a migration preserved meaning. **Still Proposed**: representation only.

### Semantic model and authoring (P6, P7)

A slab's `datumFace` is required — a 200mm floor whose *top* sits at level datum and one whose *bottom* does occupy different space. A stair stores riser *count*, since the levels fix the total rise, and its comfort limits are `PROVISIONAL` because real limits come from a jurisdiction's code profile. A material carries every property with its provenance. A schedule stores the question and never the answer.

Typing a room name and pressing `W` no longer fires the wall tool; the rule is total by default, because every candidate for a punch-through list already means something inside a text field. Splitting a wall no longer drops its doors — reassigned deterministically, or the split is blocked and the straddling opening named. Selection works without a pointer, and hidden nodes stay selectable, because a hidden object cannot be clicked at all.

### Plan, 3D, sheets, output (P9)

float32 resolves ~60mm at 1000km, so a georeferenced site snaps to a grid coarser than its own walls — origin rebasing removes AC3-070's jitter and mis-picking, tested against `Math.fround` rather than a model of the loss. Invalidation is driven by *effect*, not operation type, so a rename no longer re-meshes a building. Derived geometry declares itself underivable-from: `meshIsMeasurable` and `meshEditIsPersistable` return false unconditionally. Hiding and clipping are view properties — `visibleForSchedule` and `sectionBoxAffectsQuantities` say so in code, because a schedule agreeing with the drawing would under-order. A sheet crop is model-space, so rescaling shrinks the drawing rather than growing a west wing; annotation prints at 2.5mm at every scale. A schedule that overflows reports a count and the sheets it needs. PDF generation moved off the main thread with acknowledged cancellation, and exported bytes are read back by an independent reader that measures the printed scale rather than trusting a title block.

### Accessibility (P10)

`disabled` removes a control from the tab order, so a keyboard user never learns why it cannot be used; `aria-disabled` keeps it reachable and the resulting obligation is returned alongside the attributes. Live regions coalesce per region and never delay an assertive message. Long names truncate in the middle, because "…- Planning - REV C" and "REV D" differ at the end. `dialogFits` checks the smallest viewport and 200% text *together*, which is the case that actually breaks. Pencil ownership survives the palm lifting after the stylus — the naive rule ends the stroke at the user's wrist. `NON_COLOUR_STATE_CUES` pins that no state is carried by colour alone, which forced colours would erase.

### Language System (P11)

Everything above introduced states, refusals and reports with no entry in the governed vocabulary, so the Language System could not check any of them. Three new state machines (`view-visibility`, `section-box`, `import-units`), a `reversed` proposal state, eleven message IDs, thirteen prohibited upgrades (hidden→removed, clipped→deleted, quarantined→imported, written→published, approved→applied), three fidelity terms, and announcement profiles matching what `live-region-queue` enforces. A fourth read-only cause, `another-window-is-editing`, joins them: telling someone their file is too new when they simply have it open in another tab is a wrong answer to the only question they are asking. The full ladder passes.

### AI, plugins, interoperability, security (P12, P13)

A proposal is a request. The grant is a separate argument to `evaluateProposal`, never a field on the proposal, so no wording a model produces can widen it — three injection tests come at it from different angles. Extensions declare a closed capability set, and the host boundary is a closed union of plain serialisable messages with no variant able to carry a handle. An import whose units are unknown is refused rather than guessed. Unsupported entities are quarantined with their payload. A compressed source is bounded by ratio *while it decompresses*. Telemetry gains the allowlist half a denylist cannot provide.

### Auditing the traceability record, and what it found (P1–P3, P7)

`pre-existing` was the disposition the record itself flagged as worth reading sceptically: it meant "the repository already had the module the task names", not "the task is finished". Reading all 65 of those rows rather than trusting that caveat moved thirteen rows and found **eight real defects**. The recurring shape was a module that exists, is correct, and is well tested — wired to nothing that needed it.

- **V3-030, the single-writer lock ADR-0024 specifies, was never acquired.** `acquireSingleWriterLock` had no caller outside its own tests, so `readOnly` came only from the file's writer-version floor. Two windows could open one project writable, each believing it was the writer. The suite was green throughout, because a lock nobody takes breaks no test. The lease is now taken before the Worker is constructed — a contended project is not first imported into a working copy another context holds — and released when the session closes or the open fails.
- **V3-038, open never checked a file's own digests.** A `.arq` carries `checksums.json` recording what every entry should hash to. `verifyArqfsEntryDigests` had exactly one caller: publication. So a file this build had just written was verified, and a file from anywhere else was adopted on trust — a `model.json` edited to remain valid JSON would decode into whatever it now said and become the project. Open refuses it now, before the archive is parsed.
- **V3-021, neither Worker validated its incoming message.** `handleArqfsWorkerRequest`'s switch is exhaustive over the union, so an unrecognised `type` fell through and returned `undefined`, which the Worker posted — the caller waited out a full timeout for a request refused on arrival, contradicting that function's own documented contract.
- **V3-090, the snap sources and the layer that ranks them had no path between them.** `rankCandidates` took a `SnapResult[]` and nothing built one. `inference-engine.ts` names the gap in its own doc comment and then supplies the ranking half only.
- **V3-031**, seven structurally different import rejections reached the caller under one code — including "the source changed underneath us", which a surface must not treat as ordinarily retryable. **V3-029**, cancelling a request that was not in flight leaked its id permanently. **V3-012/V3-015**, `acquire` discarded the outgoing project. **V3-019**, import events carried no request id, so a slow first import could drive the second one's UI.

**Where the same check was wrong.** Three more hits were not defects. V3-142/V3-143's iPad shells are ARQ-030 prototypes superseded by `workspace-root.tsx`, which handles both tablet platforms itself; wiring them in would regress the shell. V3-148's keyboard bindings are implemented directly in `App.tsx`. The reachability check finds candidates, not verdicts.

**The record had a defect of its own.** Its symbol check was optional, which let four P2 rows name `workers/import-export-worker` for tasks living in the *arqfs* Worker and verify clean, because the path they named did exist. A symbol is now required. That would not have caught those four on its own — the document says so, and says what did: reading them.

Six rows are now `implemented-differently`, each with its divergence written out rather than filed as done. Byte-identity verification (V3-035) is not available through `opfs-sahpool`, which keeps no file at the name it was given; no manifest records a semantic hash for V3-039 to verify against, so that hash is computed and carried, not checked.

## Non-goals

The 28 owner-authority and 3 evidence-blocked tasks above.

No UI calls `NativeProjectSession.publish` yet. There is no export affordance in the app, and adding one is product scope this does not take on — the Worker command, the session method and the lifecycle states are in place for it.

Two tasks needed no work and were checked before writing anything: **V3-179** (`redact-sensitive-fields.ts` already recurses arrays and normalises key casing) and **V3-180** (`arqfs-support-bundle.ts` already builds its preview as data).

## Tests

3457 pass repository-wide, up from 2484. `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm format`, the language ladder after each mandated refresh (format first, refresh last), and `engineering:context:build` pass on every commit.

Three existing tests were changed, each because it over-specified relative to its own stated intent. `file-state-machine.test.ts` asserted the `publishing → published` shortcut this change closes; `registry.test.ts` pinned the workspace invariant list to exactly four entries while its comment said only that the four must still be carried; `handler.test.ts` asserted the generic `IMPORT_WORKER_FAILED` for a rejection whose own test name says which refusal it is. All three are now pinned by content.

The open-project tests now inject a writer lease. They did not before, and the real implementation correctly degrades to read-only when `navigator.locks` is absent — so under jsdom every one of them would have silently exercised that branch and asserted nothing about the writable path.

`handleArqfsWorkerRequest` is now uniformly async, so its tests await it. Per-request would have coupled callers to which request types happen to be synchronous — an implementation detail that changes the moment one grows a verification step, which is what `publish` did.

## Performance effect

One extra open, integrity check and semantic re-hash per publication, on that path only. Opening a project now also verifies its recorded per-entry digests and computes its semantic hash, over entries already read across the Worker boundary — no extra round trip. Several changes reduce work: effect-based invalidation, bounded room recomputation, and `derivationsMatch` ignoring the revision so a rename does not re-mesh a wall. The units spike measured integer-micrometre arithmetic as faster than float64.

## Accessibility effect

Substantially positive — see P10 above, plus `describeVisibility` and `describeSectionBoxEffect` answering "why can I not see this" with the rule that decided.

## Project format and migration effect

No schema change and no migration. The entry-digest check deliberately avoids a new column. `canonical-length.ts` stores nothing yet; the canonical unit decision remains open.

## Dependency and licence effect

None.

## Security and privacy effect

A reduction in trust extended to unverified bytes, model output, extensions, compressed input and — new in the later commits — Worker messages and files this build did not write. Opening a project now verifies its own recorded digests before parsing it, and both Workers validate their incoming requests rather than trusting a type annotation on a `postMessage` payload. The single-writer lock is now actually acquired. Publication runs where the independent reader can exist, rather than being simulated on the main thread. No network, credential or permission surface was widened.

## Rollback

Each commit is independently revertible and additive. Reverting the publication commit reinstates an unverified publication whose copy claims verification, so pair it with removing the claim. Reverting the entry-digest commit reinstates an open path that adopts a file without checking the digests the file itself carries; reverting the writer-lock commit reinstates two windows each believing they are the writer. Reverting the publish-wiring commit removes the browser route to publication and returns `handleArqfsWorkerRequest` to a synchronous signature, which its callers await either way.

Architecture lint reports `docs/adr/0030` for prose describing a *rejected* alternative; reproduced on a pristine tree with `git stash -u`, so it predates this branch. `verify-routes` is red for a missing `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET` — an owner action, explained in a PR comment.

title: Publication: checkpoint, export, fresh-reader verification, and a real Publish command
body:
Implements the Implementation Pack 3.0's P5 (portable publication) and closes a real, previously-unfixed async race, reconciled against the real repository rather than the revision the pack observed.

**This PR's scope changed twice while it was open.** It began as an independent implementation of the native open path; PR-294 merged the same objective mid-flight, so `6c29e70` reconciles onto the merged implementation and drops this branch's duplicates, keeping only what the merged path didn't have (a working-copy integrity check). Everything from `4abed44` onward is new: publication.

## Problem

"Opening is not saving" was `STATUS.md`'s own honest boundary. There was no way to turn an open project's working copy into a portable `.arq` file, and the pack's own rule for what counts as a publication is strict: nothing may be called published until a completely independent reader has reopened the bytes and confirmed they mean the same thing as the source.

Building the export side of the Worker protocol surfaced a real, already-shipped defect: `importDatabase`'s Worker implementation called `poolUtil.importDb(...)` — which returns a Promise — without awaiting it, then opened a fresh connection over the target file on the very next line. Nothing had caught it because every existing capability check's payload was small and fast enough for the race to usually lose.

## Solution

**Worker protocol** (`4abed44`): `exportDatabase` switches the connection out of WAL mode with `journal_mode=DELETE` (a checkpoint alone is insufficient — it merges pending frames but leaves the header still declaring WAL, caught by an adversarial test that fed checkpointed-but-not-mode-switched bytes back through the byte-level preflight) and returns the working copy's bytes. `computeSemanticHash` exposes the existing `computeProjectSemanticHash` over the protocol. `handleArqfsWorkerRequest` is now properly `async`, which is what let the import race be fixed.

**The publish pipeline** (`9e529bb`): `NativeProjectSession.prepareForPublication` drains every in-flight write through the *same* queue `save` uses — queued as a step in that chain, not a spectator of it, so a `save` issued after publish starts cannot race the export — then checkpoints and exports. `publishNativeProject` reopens those bytes through `openNativeProject` on a Worker the *caller* constructs fresh (never derived from the source session, since a fresh reader that shared state with the writer wouldn't prove anything), compares project id, revision (`#operations.length`, not the caller-overridable `journalSequence`) and semantic hash, and closes the verification session regardless of outcome.

**Wired into the product** (`dcf9d25`): "Publish project…" in the command palette and phone menu, real disabled reasons, real outcome reported through the same command-feedback region undo/redo already use.

## Non-goals

Canvas edits still don't reach `NativeProjectSession.save` — nothing in `apps/web` calls it — so publish today republishes exactly what was opened, not live edits. `STATUS.md` and the register say this plainly rather than implying more. No browser/OPFS capability check for publish exists yet (unlike `benchmark:file-open` for opening); that and the numerics/tolerance foundation (P8) are next. No GitHub, Vercel, branch, release or production state touched.

## Tests

- 2,481 tests across 266 files pass, uncached.
- 11 new Worker tests for `exportDatabase`/`computeSemanticHash` (both refusal paths, the adversarial WAL-checkpoint case, a real round-trip open of exported bytes through an independent driver).
- 11 new tests for `publishNativeProject` against the real Worker request handler over real file-backed SQLite (not hand-mocked responses): full publish with matching receipt, exactly one extra Worker constructed and released, source project untouched afterward, revision after a real edit, refusal when closed/read-only/unsaved-failure (no wasted Worker round trip), refusal with the real reason on checkpoint interruption or reopen failure, refusal — still releasing the fresh reader — when a Worker substitutes a different project's bytes, and a concurrent save landing cleanly on one side of the queue.
- Typecheck across 37 packages; ESLint, Prettier and the full language ladder clean with the governed context refreshed.
- A production build succeeds.

## Visual evidence

None — no new visual surface; the Publish command reuses existing command-palette and feedback-region components.

## Performance effect

One checkpoint + two Worker round trips (export, hash) per publish, plus a full second open pipeline for the fresh-reader verification (a second Worker, temporarily). Not measured against a large project.

## Accessibility effect

The Publish command follows the same accessible disabled-reason pattern already established for `export-dxf`, and its outcome reports through the existing accessible command-feedback region rather than a new mechanism.

## Project format and migration effect

No schema or format change. Publish never writes to the user's original selected file — only the working copy is checkpointed, and the verification reopen uses a separate scratch working copy that is closed and not persisted as the user's active project.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No new dependencies.

## Security and privacy effect

Small positive. `exportDatabase` is gated on write capability, not merely an accepted open — checkpointing physically rewrites file pages, and a file this build must not write must not have its bytes touched even to tidy them up. Nothing leaves the origin.

## Rollback

Revert the commits from `4abed44` onward. Nothing persisted changes format; a revert removes the Publish command and its pipeline, returning to "opening is not saving" with no other behavior change.

title: Bind the Vercel deployment to an approved revision, and re-measure STATUS
body:
## What changed since this PR was opened

This branch originally added a `vercel.json` that deployed the marketing site only. **PR #294 merged to base first with a materially more complete deployment**, and this PR is now the merge of that plus the one property it lacked.

#294 ships one artifact holding both public surfaces — marketing at `/`, the browser editor at `/app/` — with security headers, a three-tier cache split keyed on whether the filename carries a content hash, `/Arq/*` compatibility redirects, and `scripts/verify-vercel-routes.mjs` checking the deployed origin rather than the build. That is a strict superset of what this branch proposed.

So the `vercel.json` conflict is resolved **in favour of theirs, wholesale**, and `scripts/vercel-build.sh` is deleted.

## The one property that did not survive the swap

A hosted build clones a *branch*, not a commit. Between the moment a release is approved at some revision and the moment Vercel checks out, the branch can move — and nothing downstream notices, because the deployment reaches READY either way and the revision recorded in the proof comes from the same drifted checkout, so it agrees with itself and confirms nothing.

`scripts/build-vercel.mjs` **recorded** `sourceCommit` without ever **comparing** it to anything. It now compares against `EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA`, before any build step runs, and fails on mismatch — the same binding `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` already gets from `scripts/write-deployment-provenance.mjs`, so both hosts hold the published artifact to one rule rather than two.

An unset variable stays a pass, on purpose. A preview builds whatever its branch points at, so there is no independent expectation to check it against and requiring one would only produce a check that always passes. Set it on production; leave it unset on previews.

| Given | Expect | Verified |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA` set to a different revision | build fails before any build step runs | ✅ exit 1, no build step reached |
| `EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA` set to the checked-out revision | build proceeds to the gates | ✅ reached `arq:language:verify` |
| `EXPECTED_SOURCE_SHA` unset | build proceeds, records `sourcePinned: false` | ✅ |

The outcome is recorded as well as enforced: `deployment-source.json` and the `vercelDeployment` block in the site proof both carry `expectedCommit` and `sourcePinned`, so a reader of the deployed artifact can tell an approved release from a preview that was free to build whatever it found.

## STATUS re-measured against the merged tree

Three claims moved, and each was measured rather than adjusted.

| Claim | Was | Now |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Tests | 2,380 across 259 files | **2,453 across 264 files** |
| CI capability checks | thirteen of fourteen | **fourteen of fifteen** |
| Base revision | `7f15889` | `1cdf160` |

The substantive one: `.arq` was described as *"library-complete; not yet reachable from the product (no open-project pipeline)"*. #294 wired that pipeline through to adoption, and `pnpm benchmark:file-open` drives it against a real production build in headless Chromium — a valid project adopts and its name reaches the shell, while truncated, WAL-dependent and foreign-SQLite files are each refused with their own diagnostic. That sentence was true when written and stayed in the file after it stopped being true, which is exactly the drift STATUS exists to prevent.

The ADR-0028 entry said acceptance *"does not implement"* the pipeline *"and nothing here claims it exists"*. It exists now. What still does not exist is writing an opened project back out — there is no publish path wired in `apps/web` — so the entry says that instead of claiming a round trip nobody built.

## Docs

`docs/deployment/VERCEL.md` is rewritten. It previously documented the config this branch proposed, which no longer exists; it now documents the deployment that does, including the routing, the cache-tier reasoning, the store-pinning fix for `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_PACKAGE_INDEX_FILE`, and how to verify a change against a live origin.

## Evidence

Run over the merge, not over either side of it.

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck` | pass (37/37 packages) |
| `test` | **2,453 passed across 264 files** |
| language ladder, CI order, `sources:verify` → `audit:ci` | pass (13/13) |
| `site:build:verify` | pass, 18 routes |
| `check:decision-ids:test`, `check:decision-ids`, `--base` | pass |
| `check:toolchain-policy`, `check:workspace-registries`, `check:editor-dependency-boundaries` | pass |
| `check-secrets-test`, `check-secrets`, `zeus-guard-test` | pass |
| Engineering OS policy, fixtures, context, workflows, bindings | pass |
| `benchmark:file-open` (headless Chromium, real production build) | pass, 0 console errors |
| `benchmark:e2e-arq-open` (real Worker over OPFS) | pass, 4/4 cases, VFS `opfs-sahpool` |

`arq:language:refresh` logs `status` as the changed source set; the engineering context was rebuilt for the same reason — both were stale against the merged tree, not against this edit alone.

## Not covered

Post-deployment verification of the live preview URL was not run from this session: the sandbox proxy refuses `CONNECT` to `*.vercel.app` with 403. `.github/workflows/verify-deployment-routes.yml` runs that check from Actions, where the runner can reach the origin, and its result on this PR is the evidence — not anything asserted here.

## Rollback

Revert the merge commit. `vercel.json` and `scripts/build-vercel.mjs` return to their #294 state; the deployment keeps working, without the revision binding.

title: Extend the file flow to the full project lifecycle, with no false open
body:
## Problem

ADR-0028 is now Accepted, so the lifecycle it governs can be built. This is the state machine half.

The existing reducer stopped at `native-opening`, which means only *"the bytes passed preflight"*. Everything after — staging a copy, verifying migration on that copy, opening the Worker, hydrating, activating — had **no representation at all**. Any surface wanting to know whether a project was open had to decide for itself, from a state that did not answer the question.

## Solution

**Extended, not replaced.** A second state machine for the same flow would be two sources of truth for one question, and they would drift.

Added states: `staging`, `staged`, `migration-verified`, `worker-open`, `hydrating`, `workspace-active`, `quarantined`, `cancelled`, `project-failed`, `recovery-available`, `recovering`, `publishing`, `published`, `closed`.

Failure is **one kind with an exhaustive reason**, not a dozen near-identical kinds. Every failure leaves the flow in the same shape — nothing open, previous project untouched, a specific cause to show — and splitting that would duplicate the structure and let the cases drift. The reason is a closed union, so a new cause cannot arrive as a string nobody wrote copy for.

## Three invariants enforced in code, not by convention

**1. No false open.** `isProjectOpen` is true *only* in `workspace-active` — not `worker-open` (the Worker holds the file but no semantic state exists yet), not `hydrating` (partway through). A test asserts every earlier state answers false:

```
✓ reports no state before workspace-active as open
```

**2. Read-only survives to the end.** `writable` is decided once at Worker open and carried on the state. My first attempt kept it in a module-level `Map` — hidden mutable state inside a pure reducer. Carrying it on the state removes that, and makes a read-only file provably still read-only when the workspace activates.

**3. Last known good rides on the failure states.** A failed open, quarantine, cancellation and close all keep it, so a failure cannot silently replace the project the user already had.

## Refusing to skip

Transitions name both source state and event, so an out-of-order event is ignored rather than skipping a stage. Skipping is the dangerous direction — it is how a project reaches active without being hydrated.

| Attempt | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `worker-opened` from `staged` | stays `staged` |
| `hydrated` from `worker-open` | stays `worker-open`, `isProjectOpen` false |
| recovery completes | rejoins at `hydrating`, **not** `workspace-active` |
| `cancel` in an active workspace | ignored — cannot invent an undo that never happened |

## Copy

Every new state goes through `describeFileFlowState`, whose exhaustive switch made the compiler list exactly which states were missing. **No new copy says "open" except `workspace-active`.** Staging and migration both say the original file is not changed. Recovery says the changes are on this device and not in the project file yet.

## Tests

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `test` | **259 files, 2,389 passed** (9 new) |
| `format:check`, `lint`, `typecheck` | pass (37/37 packages) |
| language ladder incl. state-language coverage | pass |
| Engineering OS policy, fixtures, context | pass |
| `check:decision-ids`, `check:toolchain-policy` | pass |
| architecture lint, security lint, secret scan | pass |

`apps/web/src/file-handling` is a governed source set, so the language context was refreshed in the same change — the freshness gate caught it before CI did.

## Non-goals

**This is the state machine only.** It is not wired to the Worker yet, so no surface claims a project can be opened and STATUS.md is unchanged on that point. Wiring, the browser evidence matrix, and the UI states follow in their own changes.

## Rollback

Ordinary revert. No schema, migration, dependency or lockfile change. Existing states and transitions are untouched, so the current file-open behaviour is unaffected.

Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.62.1

Bug Fixes

  • #41989 [Regression]: tsconfig "extends" bare specifier isn't resolved via node_modules walk-up like tsc (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41998 [Regression]: directory-form tsconfig project references ("path": "../pkg") fail to resolve (fatal since 1.62)
  • #41985 Accessibility snapshot drops button name when text is nested inside spans with aria-hidden SVG
  • #42000 [Regression]: page.evaluate() arg of a branded primitive type (string & { brand }) no longer type-checks since 1.62
  • #42013 [BUG]Image-type actionable elements are not presented in the snapshot.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });
await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.
await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

title: Read the reference project format, and fix two defects in opening it
body:
## What happened to this PR

It opened as a second implementation of native `.arq` open, built on a memory-resident read-only connection while ADR-0028 was still Proposed. While it was open, #294 landed the same feature on the base branch from a different architecture — an OPFS working copy under the now-Accepted ADR-0030.

Two open pipelines in one app is not a merge result worth having, so the base's is the one that survives. This PR is reduced to what #294 does not already have, plus two defects found while integrating.

**Deleted from this branch**, because #294 covers them: the memory-resident pipeline (`native-open-pipeline`, `open-native-project`, `active-project`, `arqfs-worker-transport`, `arqfs-selected-bytes-db`) and this branch's additions to the arqfs Worker protocol, handler, client and entry. The base's versions are taken wholesale, including its read gating and its `-wal` sidecar refusal.

## The reference project format

`decodeNativeProjectModel` required a root `projectName`. The real Arq model has none — it carries a project summary with its own id, name, units and revision, plus levels, wall types, rooms and views. So the shipped product could open the files it had written and refused the reference fixture outright:

```
model.json has no project name
```

It now falls back to `@arq/project-loading` when the flat shape is absent, and reports which shape arrived rather than flattening both. A project carrying a reference document gets a project browser: its levels with real per-level wall and room counts, its own model tree, an inspector reading through real wall types, level switching and close.

## Two defects the browser check found

**Choosing the open project reported that it could not be opened.** The working copy is content-addressed, so the same bytes name the same OPFS file and the same dedicated Worker file. Adoption closes the previous session only after the new open succeeds — correct, because a failed open must leave the previous project untouched — so the second Worker tried to take a working copy the live one still held. The product said "could not be opened" about a project sitting on screen.

`openNativeProject` now compares the content-addressed id against the working copy the workspace holds, before any Worker is constructed, and answers `already-open`. Both adoption-boundary guarantees survive. The comparison is keyed off a working-copy id tracked for every open, not off the project browser's model — that only exists for files carrying a reference document, and keying it there would have left the flat shape this build writes still able to hit it.

**Every level was drawn at once.** The snapshot carries all 79 walls across three levels and the plan drew all of them, so switching level changed nothing: the ground and upper floors had byte-identical pixel checksums because the upper floor was already on top. The surfaces are now fed the level on show. The project's own wall ids are carried through unchanged, because they are what the model tree selects by and what 3D highlights by.

## Claims retired

Three things this branch used to say are no longer true and are not carried forward.

- The panel said **"Read-only."** The base's working copy is writable. It now says "Working copy." and where a change actually lands: nothing is written back to the `.arq` file the reader chose.
- `benchmark:native-open` asserted the **wall tool is disabled**. It should not be — the project has somewhere to put a wall. The check now asserts the shell never claims "Saved locally", which is the claim that would genuinely be false.
- `workersAfterThreeOpens === 1` was worded as proving **each replacement terminates the one before**. It never did; all three opens were the same file. It now states what it proves — that re-choosing the open project reuses the session — and additionally asserts the re-choose is not reported as a failure.

Four tracked capability results were evidence for the deleted architecture (`wallToolDisabled: true`, a limitation naming a "read-only open") or were the failing intermediate from fixing the reopen defect. They are removed; the green run of the shipped behaviour stays, and the failing run stays in git history.

## Also fixed

Closing a project cleared the browser panel but left the project's walls, name and save state in the workspace — the reader was told nothing was open while still looking at a project.

`benchmark:native-open`'s open wait raced the dialog: it waited for the dialog's own status line, but adoption closes the dialog the instant that line becomes true, so the wait could pass or fail on render ordering alone. It passed locally and failed on CI for exactly that reason. It now waits on the project panel's header, which persists for as long as the project is open, and on a genuine timeout it distinguishes "the dialog refused the open" from "the dialog closed but the workspace never showed the project."

## Evidence

All re-run on the merged tree, not inherited, and confirmed on GitHub Actions - not only locally.

- 2,500 tests across 266 files pass.
- `pnpm typecheck` across all 37 workspace packages; lint and `format:check` clean.
- The nine governed-language verifiers and `arq:language:audit:ci` pass; context refreshed and bundled in the same change, as STATUS.md is a governed source set.
- The five Engineering OS checks pass; `zeus-guard-test` passes its 23 cases.
- `pnpm benchmark:native-open` returns `ok: true` with zero failures in headless Chromium against the vite-built bundle and the unmodified golden fixture: opens at revision 191, the ground floor reports its 37 of 79 walls, switching level changes the plan's pixel checksum (`1978175094` → `1255006032`), a wall selected from the model tree by the project's own id shows 8,458 green-dominant pixels in 3D, the shell states the working copy and never "Saved locally", three opens leave one Worker and closing leaves none, no request leaves the origin, and the fixture's SHA-256 is identical before and after.
- New unit tests pin the `already-open` answer and the case it must not swallow: a different working copy while one is open is still a real open.
- **CI on head `4420ef8`: 14 of 15 checks green** - classify, preflight, build, test, lint-and-typecheck, browser-capability-checks, language-system, rust-test, dependency-licence-scan, secret-scan, critical-approval, selected-evidence, engineering-gate, and the Vercel preview all pass.

## Not proven

Checkpointing edits into the working copy, exporting back to the `.arq` file, migration, non-native import, sync, MCP reachability, and any browser engine other than Chromium. Opening is not saving, and no surface in this change says otherwise.

## Performance

Measured on this tree. Start-up chunk 647.17 kB raw (203.53 kB gzipped); the 3D surface is a 521.04 kB deferred chunk. The SQLite Worker (237.00 kB) and `sqlite3.wasm` (864.75 kB) are fetched only when a project is actually opened. The start-up chunk remains above Vite's 500 kB warning threshold and no budget gate is wired, which STATUS records as open work.

## The one red check: `verify-routes`

Not fixable from this branch. Its own output on this PR:

> the origin is protected, so its files were never visible to this check (HTTP 200 with "sso-api"). Deployment protection is on for this origin, and no bypass token was supplied, so every path returns the sign-in page instead of the deployment. The routing contract is therefore Not inspected: this job fails because it could gather no evidence, not because a route is wrong.

It needs `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET` set as a repository secret (Vercel project settings → Deployment Protection → Protection Bypass for Automation) before it can produce real evidence. It fails identically on the base branch, for reasons unrelated to this diff.

## A note on the gate

The green Engineering OS gate does not include a human approval. `protected_l4_approval` reports `success` with state `requires-github-environment` — a deferred environment gate, not an approval anybody granted. That is recorded independently in `engineering/36_REQUIRED_CHECK_ROLLOUT.md` and applies to every L4 lane, not to this branch specially.

title: Owner decisions, identifier enforcement, and deployment provenance
body:
## Problem

PR 01 of the blocker-closure programme. Every later workstream depends on decisions that were recorded as Proposed and on identifiers that nothing enforced. This establishes that base and **deliberately implements no project-open code**.

## Owner decisions recorded

- **ADR-0028 Proposed → Accepted** (D-024). SQLite in an ARQ-owned dedicated Worker over OPFS owns the canonical local working project. IndexedDB is bounded to recovery bridging, source provenance, last-known-good pointers, resumable publication metadata, device preferences and replaceable derived caches during migration. **A journal append is not a portable save.**
- **ADR-0029 adopts `main`** as the stable integration and production branch (D-025), through a reversible migration that keeps the current branch undeleted through a rollback window. **The migration is not performed here.**

Acceptance unblocks the open pipeline. It does not implement it, and STATUS.md still says so.

## Identifier enforcement

Those decisions are worth exactly as much as the ids that carry them, and nothing checked them.

`scripts/verify-decision-ids.mjs` runs in two modes. Tree mode is the obvious one. **Base mode is the one that matters:** draft PR #280 adds a second `ADR-0027` and redefines `D-024`, and it is *internally consistent on its own branch* — so a tree-only check passes it. Only comparing against the base shows both ids were taken by work that merged first.

The self-test asserts that asymmetry on a real git history:

```
PASS the collision branch passes a tree-only check, which is why it was missed
PASS the collision branch fails the base comparison
PASS the base comparison names the reused ADR file id
PASS the base comparison names the redefined decision
```

**Two design corrections, both found by the check rejecting legitimate work and both pinned as regression tests:**

1. Exact text equality rejected accepting D-024 in place, because its text began with the word "Proposed". A check that blocks ordinary governance gets switched off.
2. Jaccard similarity was tried next and was also wrong — it scores *adding detail* as low as *replacing* the decision. The rule now uses an overlap coefficient.

## Toolchain policy

`engines.node` was `">=20"` with no upper bound — a claim that every future Node major works, while every workflow pins 20. Now `">=20 <23"`, the range actually exercised. `scripts/verify-toolchain-policy.mjs` fails if a workflow steps outside it or overrides the pnpm pin. The unbounded range is what the check caught first.

## Deployment provenance

A hosted build clones a *branch*, so it can move between approval and checkout. The footer revision comes from the same drifted checkout, agrees with itself, and confirms nothing.

The expected SHA now arrives from the event rather than the working tree, a mismatch **fails the Pages job before upload**, and the artifact carries a provenance record with both SHAs, toolchain, per-route and per-file hashes.

| mode | result |
| --- | --- |
| expected SHA matches | pass |
| expected SHA differs | **fail**, names both SHAs |
| expected SHA unset | **fail** |
| unset + explicit preview opt-out | pass |

Provenance is written even on failure, because a blocked release is exactly when the record is needed.

## Verified facts replacing reported ones

The GitHub API returns `visibility: public`, `private: false`, `allow_forking: true`, `license: NOASSERTION`, while `LICENSE` says "proprietary and confidential".

The proprietary grant is **untouched** — that is the owner's decision with legal advice. "Confidential" is a claim about who can read the repository, and it is contradicted by the repository being publicly readable and forkable by anyone. Both resolutions and their consequences are recorded in `LICENSE-DECISION-REQUIRED.md` for the owner to choose. No public surface states a licence position.

## Engineering OS rollout

`engineering/36_REQUIRED_CHECK_ROLLOUT.md` records what must hold before the gate becomes required — including that its own `protected_l4_approval` currently resolves to a **deferred environment gate rather than an approval anybody granted**, and that one green run is not a rollout criterion.

## Tests

All uncached at this tree:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `format:check`, `lint` | pass |
| `typecheck` | 37/37 packages plus `contracts/` |
| `test` | **259 files, 2,380 passed, 0 failed** |
| architecture lint, security lint | pass |
| `check:decision-ids` + self-test | pass (11 assertions) |
| `check:toolchain-policy` | pass |
| Engineering OS policy, fixtures, context, bindings, workflows | pass |
| language ladder + `arq:language:audit:ci` | pass |
| `arq:language:site:build:verify` | pass |

## Non-goals

No project-open pipeline. No branch migration. No licence grant change. No repository setting changed. No deployment.

## Rollback

Ordinary revert. No schema, migration, canonical operation, dependency or lockfile change.
