title: Native .arq project opening and repository-native Vercel deployment
body:
## Problem

Reconciled from the ARQ Native Project Open and Vercel Implementation Pack v2.0 (SHA-256 `0a62e551…`, checksum verified) against this repository. The pack is evidence, not authority — live implementation and accepted ADRs outrank it (`.zeus/INVARIANTS.md`), and each proposal was checked for an existing equivalent, ADR conflict, and whether it would create a second source of truth.

Three defects confirmed by reading the live code rather than trusting the pack:

1. **`arqfs-worker-handler.ts` gated writes but not reads.** `getArchiveEntry` and `listArchiveEntryPaths` called straight through to the store. A Worker holding an open driver would hand back project bytes for a file it had never opened — and for a file whose open it had explicitly *rejected*, since rejection leaves the driver connected and records a verdict those paths never read.
2. **A database missing its `-wal` sidecar was presented as openable.** SQLite opens it without error and serves the last checkpoint, so the user sees an apparently healthy project silently missing their most recent saved work. The product showed a caution next to it.
3. **`ArqfsWorkerRequestInput` was `Omit`.** `keyof` a union is only the keys common to all members, so it collapsed to `{ type }` and discarded `path` and `entries` — every parameterized Worker request was untypeable.

Verified absent from the repository at the fork point: `apps/web/src/project/`, `packages/arqfs/src/arqfs-source-completeness.ts`, `vercel.json`.

## Solution

Choosing a `.arq` file now opens it. The byte-level checks run first and refuse before anything is constructed — a refusal must not cost an OPFS working copy — then the bytes are imported into a working copy via a new `importDatabase` Worker command (`opfs-sahpool` keeps databases in opaque pool files, so this has to go through `poolUtil.importDb` inside the Worker entry), opened through sqlite-wasm, decoded, and adopted into the workspace.

Every failure past Worker construction releases it. A leaked Worker holds the OPFS write lock on its working copy and makes that project unopenable for the rest of the session, so that is the property the tests assert on each rejection — not just the returned code.

Adoption is the caller's, never the panel's: the workspace replaces its project only once a candidate is fully decoded, so a rejected or cancelled file leaves whatever was already open untouched.

### Opening is not saving

Nothing checkpoints edits back to the `.arq` file. The workspace reports the project as open and not saved, because saying `saved` would claim durability this build has not earned. Copy-on-write migration stays unreachable for the same reason, and `canMigrate` is treated as **read-only** rather than as permission to write (ADR-0030).

## Non-goals

- No merge, no production promotion. GitHub Pages stays live as the rollback host and is untouched.
- No write-back, checkpointing or export to the chosen file.
- No copy-on-write migration made user-reachable.
- No public `ARQ`/`Arq` casing change — that conflict belongs to the Language System's owner.
- No import/export UI, sync backend, or MCP product surface.

## Tests

Baseline before any change: typecheck exit 0, 259 files / 2362 tests.
Current: **typecheck exit 0, 264 files / 2444 tests**, lint 0, format clean, both generated contexts verifying fresh.

New coverage: Worker read-gate tests, source-completeness tests, native-project-core tests, and the open pipeline's own failure paths.

## Browser evidence

`pnpm benchmark:file-open` — real production bundle in headless Chromium, four real fixtures built by the Node arqfs driver.

| Fixture | Outcome |
|---|---|
| valid project | adopted; workspace shows **"Capability check project"**, dialog dismissed |
| truncated | refused, `ARQ_FILE_TRUNCATED` |
| non-Arq SQLite | refused, `NOT_ARQ_SQLITE` |
| WAL project without its `-wal` sidecar | refused, `ARQ_WAL_SIDECAR_REQUIRED`, remedy included |

`ok: true`, no console errors, no unserved requests.

The accepting case asserts the **workspace**, not the panel's own message. Opening is terminal in this product — adoption dismisses the dialog — so the panel's "… is open." exists only as long as the dialog does. The top bar showing the project's own name is the stronger claim anyway: it proves the Worker was constructed, the bytes imported, the database opened through sqlite-wasm, the archive decoded and the model adopted.

The WAL fixture is the one that matters most: a real write-ahead-log project copied while the connection is open and SQLite has **not** checkpointed — the exact state a file picker hands over. This instrument had no WAL fixture at all before, so it passed identically before and after the policy changed, and could not have told anyone whether the policy worked.

## Performance effect

Start-up **627.56 kB (198.06 kB gzip)**, with the 3D surface deferred to a 520.88 kB chunk. Wiring the open path added ~13.6 kB to start-up; the Worker (237.11 kB) and sqlite-wasm (864.75 kB) load only when a project is opened. The chunk-size warning threshold was not raised to silence anything.

## Accessibility effect

Label-in-Name holds on the file chooser (visible text contained in accessible name), asserted in the browser check. Every refusal is a text failure state with a real diagnostic code behind a disclosure, not a colour-only signal. A project that opened read-only says so and carries the reason, rather than silently refusing edits.

## Project format and migration effect

No `.arq` schema change. Selected source bytes are never edited in place — the working copy is a separate OPFS database seeded from a copy. The IndexedDB journal remains a device-local recovery tier and is not described as a portable `.arq` save.

## Dependency and licence effect

One workspace dependency added: `@arq/project-format` to `@arq/web`. Browser-safe (Web Crypto, no `node:` imports) and on no editor dependency boundary's forbidden list.

## Security and privacy effect

The read gate is a genuine confidentiality fix: project bytes were readable from a file this build had rejected. Security headers on every path. `secret-scan` passes.

## Deployment effect

Vercel builds from the checked-out commit and writes provenance into the artifact. Diagnosed from the real build log: builds failed with `ERR_PNPM_MISSING_PACKAGE_INDEX_FILE` for `canvaskit-wasm` because Vercel restores `node_modules` from its build cache while pnpm's global store lives outside it, and `check-dependency-licences.mjs` reads the store. **This affected every branch including production, not just this PR.** Fixed by pinning one store for install and every nested pnpm; all three connected Vercel projects now build Ready.

`scripts/verify-vercel-routes.mjs` is the routing half of deployment verification (`/app/`, deep-route fallback, `/Arq/*` 308, real 404 status, cache split, security headers, provenance commit). Deliberately separate from `verify-arq-deployed-public-site.mjs`, which owns the copy proof.

## Known blockers

1. **Preview route verification is Blocked, and the cause is now verified rather than inferred.** The check reports `HTTP 200 with "sso-api"` — Vercel Deployment Protection serves a sign-in page at every path, so the deployment's own files were never visible to it. Routing is therefore **Not inspected**; it is not failing and it is not passing. To make it verifiable: Vercel project settings → Deployment Protection → *Protection Bypass for Automation*, then store the value as the `VERCEL_AUTOMATION_BYPASS_SECRET` repository secret, which this script already sends. Owner action.
2. **Two surplus Vercel projects** (`arq-editor-preview`, `arq-file-format-test`) still build this repository on every push and pick up the new `vercel.json`. `arq-website` is canonical. Removing them is a dashboard action.

## Rollback

Every slice is independently revertible. Reverting the deployment slice removes `vercel.json` and the build script; Pages continues unchanged because `deploy-pages.yml` is untouched. The native-open slices revert without downgrading any ARQFS safety behaviour — foreign-key policy, writer lock and the new read gates are separable from the UI change.

title: Reconcile the ARQ package audit against the real repository
body:
## Problem

A reconciliation candidate was produced against audited base `7f15889`, but it was assembled in a sandbox with **synthetic Git ancestry** and no pnpm, Prettier or Rust toolchain. Several of its recorded passes did not hold in a real checkout, and one recorded failure was an artifact of the synthetic history rather than a real defect.

This repository's HEAD was still `7f15889` — the exact audited base. The remote never moved, and the candidate `9a3f5d5` was never pushed. So the reconciliation remained applicable and needed verifying against a genuine tree.

## Solution

Four commits.

**1. Reconciliation (`f1e1515`)** — unchanged in substance:

- canonical URLs on all generated marketing routes, `noindex, nofollow` on 404, headings visible without entrance animation, build revision bound to `SITE_REVISION`, stale date and revision labels removed
- MCP recorded as a library-only proposal boundary, not a product feature
- ARQ made canonical in public prose; lowercase `arq` kept for code identifiers, packages, routes and the `.arq` extension; the case-sensitive `/Arq` Pages path preserved
- marketing layout changes mapped into Engineering OS evidence selection, with a classifier regression fixture
- ADR-0028 added as **Proposed**, not Accepted

Corrections only a real repository run could expose:

- **`format:check` failed on the three files this change adds** (ADR-0028, the audit, the matrix JSON). Every pre-existing file passed. This would have failed CI.
- **Two generated contexts then went stale** (Engineering OS and language), because formatting changed the `docs/adr` digest. Regenerated through their own generators, never hand-edited.
- **Narrowed the security-lint change.** It had exempted every `*.test.*` and `*.spec.*` file from *both* SQLite rules and skipped the extension rule on any line containing a negation word — wider than the "narrow, reviewed allowance" it was described as, and it would have let a future test enable `PRAGMA trusted_schema = ON` undetected. Per-line scoping is kept; the four legitimate sites in `packages/arqfs` carry explicit site-local `security-lint: allow` markers.
- **Corrected STATUS.md**, which asserted 2,362 passing tests and twelve capability checks. Measured: 2,380 tests across 259 files, and CI wires thirteen of the fourteen capability checks (`benchmark:arq-core-worker` is defined but not run).
- The strict repository-binding check, the candidate's single recorded failure, **passes here** with status `ready`, zero errors and zero warnings.

**2. STATUS accuracy (`5197120`)** — record the CI-executed Rust and capability gates.

**3. Bundle split (`30f66a8`)** — the package's bundle finding (REC-020) was marked blocked only because the sandbox could not build. Measured here: `1,136.33 kB` raw / `325.72 kB` gzipped, byte-identical to the recorded figure, so it was still current rather than stale. `ModelCanvas` carries three.js and is only rendered for the `3d` tab, so it now loads via `lazy`/`Suspense` when that tab first opens.

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| start-up raw | 1,136.33 kB | **613.85 kB** (−46%) |
| start-up gzip | 325.72 kB | **193.31 kB** (−40.7%) |

The deferred chunk is 520.88 kB (132.18 kB gzipped). The split follows the surface boundary that already existed; no `manualChunks` and no arbitrary boundaries.

**4. Gate hole (`c6268a8`)** — found by walking into it. `browser_model_canvas` is keyed on `ModelCanvas.tsx`, but commit 3 changed **only `App.tsx`**, which is where the viewport decides which surface mounts and how it loads. The gate selected 23 evidence items, ten of them browser checks, and the model-canvas check was not among them: the check that established 3D reachability was not required by the change that altered how 3D loads. The mapping is added to `editor-shell-and-accessibility` and pinned by classifier fixture 23. Confirmed in CI — selection rose to 24 and `browser_model_canvas` now appears with `"result": "success"`.

## Non-goals

- No merge, no deployment, no release or production-readiness claim.
- ADR-0028 is **not** promoted to Accepted. The SQLite/OPFS versus IndexedDB responsibility split still needs an owner decision, so the user-reachable `.arq` open lifecycle is deliberately not implemented here.
- No canonical operation, schema, migration, file-format version or dependency was changed.
- No catalogue expansion.

## Visual evidence

Playwright Chromium over a local HTTP server serving `dist` under `/Arq`, so assets resolve over **real HTTP** rather than being inlined: 18 routes across 1440×900, 834×1112 and 390×844 with `reducedMotion: reduce`.

**54 route/viewport checks, 0 findings.** No horizontal overflow, exactly one visible H1 per route (proving heading visibility without entrance animation), canonical present, landmarks present, no missing image alt, no unnamed controls, no empty links, visible initial keyboard focus, no console errors, no failed requests, no em dashes.

Rendered output: canonical 18/18, 404 `noindex, nofollow`, `/Arq` base path applied, footer bound to the real build revision via `SITE_REVISION`, no standalone title-case product name in visible text.

## Tests

Local, uncached:

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `pnpm format:check` | pass |
| `pnpm lint` | pass |
| `pnpm typecheck` | 37/37 packages plus `contracts/` |
| `pnpm test` | **259 files, 2,380 passed, 0 failed** |
| architecture lint / security lint | pass |
| secret scan and self-test | pass |
| workspace registries, editor boundaries, dependency licences | pass |
| Engineering OS policy, fixtures, context, bindings, workflows | pass |
| language ladder (13 steps) plus `arq:language:audit:ci` | pass |
| marketing build under the real deployment environment | 18 routes |
| `arq:language:site:build:verify` | pass |
| `benchmark:model-canvas`, `workspace-layout`, `wall-hud`, `network-observation` | pass |

Two negative controls: the narrowed security lint still catches new violations in a test file, and fixture 23 fails with `evidence missing: browser_model_canvas` if the mapping is removed.

Confirmed in CI at `c6268a8`: `build`, `test`, `lint-and-typecheck`, `rust-test`, `browser-capability-checks`, `language-system`, `secret-scan`, `dependency-licence-scan`, `classify`, `preflight`, `critical-approval`, `selected-evidence` — 13 of 14 green.

**Not run, so not claimed:** deployed-site verification, protected L4 approval, physical iPad/Pencil/RoomPlan/LiDAR/Safari/Firefox evidence.

## Performance effect

Measured, not inherited — see commit 3 above. Start-up JavaScript drops 46% raw and 40.7% gzipped by deferring the 3D surface.

`benchmark:model-canvas` still activates the real `3D` tab, renders through WebGL2 and shares selection with the plan canvas in both directions (17,357 green-dominant pixels on select, 0 after clearing) with zero console errors. `benchmark:network-observation` exercises "switched to the 3D view", so it observes the new runtime fetch: **9 requests, all same-origin, 0 off-device**. Deferring a chunk did not weaken the privacy observation.

The start-up chunk is still above Vite's 500 kB warning threshold and no budget gate is wired, so bundle size remains open work rather than closed.

## Accessibility effect

No regressions across the 54 rendered checks: landmarks, single visible H1, image alt text, control naming, link text, visible initial focus and reduced-motion behaviour all pass. The `Suspense` fallback reuses the `role="status"` / `aria-live="polite"` pattern already used by the file panel.

## Project format and migration effect

None. No `.arq` schema, file-format version, migration, journal, recovery implementation or publication path was modified.

The `packages/arqfs` edits are **comment-only** — `security-lint: allow` markers at sites the lint must not flag. No executable behaviour changed, confirmed by the suite passing unchanged at 2,380 tests and by `browser_arqfs_opfs`, `browser_arqfs_writer_lock`, `browser_arqfs_project_isolation` and `browser_journal_recovery` passing in CI.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No dependency added, removed or upgraded; `pnpm-lock.yaml` unchanged; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` succeeds at 287 packages.

Unresolved and **not** addressed here: the repository is public while `LICENSE` describes contents as proprietary and confidential and `LICENSE-DECISION-REQUIRED.md` records a private-repository intent. That is an owner and legal decision.

## Security and privacy effect

Net strengthening, twice.

The security-lint change as proposed would have left every test and spec file permanently unscanned for both SQLite rules — material in a repository whose central invariant is safe handling of untrusted `.arq` files. Both blanket heuristics are removed and replaced with four explicit, diff-visible, site-local allow markers, each individually reviewed and legitimate: an adversarial test that sets `PRAGMA trusted_schema = ON` precisely to prove the open policy forces it back off, a test asserting `load_extension()` is rejected, and a doc comment describing that rejection.

Separately, the evidence gate no longer lets a change to the surface that mounts the 3D view skip the 3D proof.

Public claim surfaces were tightened, not widened. No new capability, availability, cross-platform, lossless or production-readiness claim is introduced.

## Rollback

Nothing is merged or deployed, so rollback is a branch operation only:

```
git reset --hard 7f15889
```

No remote default branch, no deployment and no user project data has been affected. No project-data rollback is required because no project-data code changed. Individual commits are independently revertable; reverting commit 3 also warrants reverting commit 4, since fixture 23 exists because of it.

If this is ever merged and deployed, roll back by rebuilding the last known good source SHA through the protected Pages workflow, then re-verify routes, metadata, responsive layout, focus, console, network and revision attribution.

## Known red

`engineering-gate` fails on **`e2e_arq_open`** only (24 selected, 23 passed, `"Proof gap is not closed."`). It needs the browser Worker and OPFS project-open proof, which is blocked on ADR-0028. Not honestly fixable in this PR.

`protected_l4_approval` reports `"result": "success"` with `"state": "requires-github-environment"`. That is a deferred environment gate, not an approval anyone granted, and nothing here treats it as one.

Vercel checks fail on every commit of this branch, including commits that change nothing the failing projects consume. There is no Vercel configuration in the repository and PR #292 had no Vercel checks at all, so this is pre-existing setup rather than a regression from this branch.

## Owner decisions still required

1. **ADR-0028** — accept, revise or reject the persistence responsibility split. This gates the `.arq` open lifecycle and everything sequenced behind it.
2. **Repository visibility versus licence wording.**
3. **Draft PR #280** — stale: based on older state and using ADR-0027 for a desktop-shell decision while current ADR-0027 governs the MCP boundary. Close or rebuild.

title: MCP System 3.0: the AI boundary, wired to the real Arq packages (ADR-0027)
body:
## Problem

Two MCP reference packages were supplied for review (`ARQ_MCP_SYSTEM_1.0`, `ARQ_MCP_SYSTEM_2.0`). Their safety instincts were right - no raw file writing, no database access, no model-controlled approval, no broad execute tool - and they had one crippling limitation: they were written without this repository. Every page carried the same blocker, _"the actual ARQ repository and runtime contracts were not supplied"_.

So the 2.0 adapter validated a fixture operation called `fixture.record.put` against a `Map` of strings, its capability report said `semantic_geometry: unavailable`, its own integration plan warned "do not hand-maintain a second list in TypeScript" while shipping exactly that, and the domain-profile system at the centre of its architecture - a ten-row contract, an ADR, a coverage tool meaningless without it - existed only in prose. On top of that it carried a set of real defects: a `provenance` field the model itself wrote, a reference-URI guard that was a prefix test, an unbounded idempotency map, a public commit method on the adapter the tool layer held, coverage that ignored version, project state and scopes, and seven of eleven declared proposal states that nothing could reach.

## Solution

`packages/mcp-server`, inside the monorepo and wired to the packages that already exist.

- **Operation types come from `@arq/arqscript`'s own constructors** (ADR-0014), read at module load, so a rename there fails a test here rather than leaving the catalogue describing an operation that no longer exists.
- **The model is `@arq/bim-core`**; validation is `@arq/validation` and `@arq/operations`. A wall shorter than a millimetre, a self-intersecting room boundary and two openings sharing a span are refused by the rules that already exist.
- **Derived-output names are bim-core's own invalidation constants**, not a second spelling.
- **A domain-profile registry** with a registered `architecture` profile and a `declared_unregistered` `vehicle.concept` profile. A request Arq cannot serve returns the profile that would own the work, the five operations it would need and seven named blockers - a reviewable backlog instead of a refusal or a fuselage called a wall.
- **The Review Centre as tested code**: header copy, action availability with a mandatory reason, tab visibility, the accessible impact summary, and a persistence vocabulary that never answers "saved".
- **Zero new dependencies.** The MCP protocol, the schema layer and both transports are implemented here.

Wiring ArqScript to bim-core surfaced three real gaps in ArqScript v0, recorded on the operations concerned rather than papered over: `create wall` has no level while `createWall` requires one; the wall type is a display name where the model needs an identified type with a thickness; `create room` supplies a polygon while `Room` carries a calculated boundary, area and status.

The full defect register - 10 security, 14 correctness, 5 resource, 6 architecture - is in `docs/ai/MCP-SYSTEM-3.0-PLAN.md`.

## Beyond the MCP boundary

Reviewing the packages this one has to trust turned up defects in already-shipped code. Each was reproduced against the source before being touched, and each fix is proven by running the real tooling rather than by inspection.

**File integrity.** The `.arq` semantic hash concatenated path and content without length framing, so two different projects could hash identically - proven with a runnable collision before the fix, and the regression test proven non-vacuous by showing v1 collides where v2 does not. The arqfs worker asked `openArqfs` whether it could write and then ignored the answer, so a file this build had just declared itself unqualified to write could be mutated by the next message. The defensive open policy had no non-test caller, so `PRAGMA foreign_keys` stayed off in the real browser runtime and every `REFERENCES` the schema declares was inert. The single-writer lock used one global name, so opening project A blocked project B, and discarded the request's own rejection, so a refusal hung for ever instead of degrading. Byte preflight read the write-ahead-log header and returned it, but nothing drew the conclusion: SQLite opened without a `-wal` sidecar returns the database as of its last checkpoint rather than failing, so a picked `project.arq` could show a compatible, healthy project missing the user's newest work. A failed copy-on-write migration deleted the corrupt copy - the only evidence of a bug that corrupts projects during upgrade - and can now quarantine it instead.

**Privacy.** `redactSensitiveFields` matched exact camelCase only, so `project_name` passed through untouched, and declined to recurse into arrays, so `{ walls: [{ geometry: ... }] }` leaked entirely - a test asserted that leak as intended behaviour. Both closed.

**Accessibility.** The status bar carried `role="status" aria-live="polite"` on its own `<footer>`, so every child announced itself on change including the cursor position, which changes on every pointer move. A polite region queues rather than interrupts, so a screen reader would read coordinates for ever and reach nothing else.

**Gate integrity.** The scripts that produce and check the gate's evidence classified as `unknown_runtime_surface`, so editing the wasm parity checker never selected `wasm_parity` - the check could be weakened in the change it was meant to measure. `wasm_parity` and `worker_core` both read a build artifact no workflow built, so both failed at "pkg does not exist" for every change that selected them, measuring the runner rather than the diff. `verify-workflow-templates.mjs` read reference templates this repository correctly never installed, threw `ENOENT` on every invocation and was wired to nothing. Six passing capability checks had no catalog id, so the gate could not select the single-writer lock check when the single-writer lock changed. `packages/mcp-server` itself - the AI trust boundary - had no change-map rule at all.

**Privacy transport.** `DRIFT-PRIVACY-TRANSPORT-ABSOLUTE` blocked the claim `no-network-data-transfer` at high severity for want of an instrument. `benchmark:network-observation` now records every request the real bundle attempts in headless Chromium while a wall is drawn, the 3D view opened and the file panel used, and fails if any leaves the origin that served it. It records rather than blocks, because blocking outbound traffic and observing none measures the harness; attempts count rather than successes; and it fails if nothing at all was observed. Proven by injecting a real `fetch` to an external host, catching it, and removing it. **The conflict stays open** - its resolution needs the test *and* an approved privacy statement, and the statement is the registry owner's decision.

## Non-goals

Nothing here is reachable from the product, and STATUS.md says so.

- No React surface consumes the Review Centre model; the Assistant panel is not built.
- `apps/web` does not implement `ArqProjectHost`; the host in this PR holds the model in memory.
- No `.arq` file is written. Publication stays a request the operator completes in Arq.
- No client run has been recorded. The templates in `config/` are starting points, and support is claimed per client after a run, never inferred.
- No remote gateway, authorization server or tenancy. `arq_get_capabilities` reports `remote_gateway` as unavailable.

## Known-failing check

`engineering-gate` fails, and should. Its decision on `a604920` is **33 evidence selected, 32 passed, 1 failed**, with no `needs_review` and no `missing_mappings`.

The single failure is `e2e_arq_open`, a declared proof gap (`kind: "proof-gap"`, `state: "missing"`). Its catalog closure is "wire a real browser Worker and OPFS project-opening flow, then test valid, old-reader, corrupt, and read-only outcomes" - and STATUS.md records that pipeline as **blocked on an open owner decision**, `DECISION-PERSISTENCE-TIERS`, which "needs an explicit ADR resolution before the open-project pipeline is built". So the gap cannot be closed here without pre-empting a decision the repository reserves to its owner, and the only other route to green - lowering the catalog state - is what `30_ZEUS_AND_ENGINEERING_AUTHORITY.md` forbids. It is left reporting the truth.

The gate runs in shadow mode and is not a required check; GitHub reports this PR as `mergeable_state: unstable`, not `blocked`.

## Visual evidence

None. This PR adds no rendered surface. `review/review-centre.ts` is the state, copy and action-gating model a panel would render, covered by 18 tests. The accessibility fix above is asserted in the real DOM by `benchmark:workspace-layout` rather than by screenshot, because this repository has no component-test stack and "which element is a live region" is a rendering fact.

## Tests

**2,362 tests across 259 files**, all passing; 256 of them new in `packages/mcp-server`.

Several are structural rather than example-based, which is the point:

- The tool table and the scope table must be equal in **both** directions, so a tool cannot be added without a scope and a scope cannot linger without a tool.
- Every declared proposal state must be reachable by walking the transition graph.
- The advertised limits must equal the enforced ones.
- An ungranted project and a nonexistent one must produce byte-identical errors.
- Fourteen hostile reference URIs that the 2.0 guard accepted are pinned as failing.
- A full client journey from `initialize` through to a queued proposal, asserting `canonicalMutation: none` at every step.
- Five new classifier fixtures pin the gate changes; each was shown to fail when its rule is removed.

## Performance effect

None on the product; nothing imports `packages/mcp-server` yet. Within the package: response size is capped at 256 KiB per tool result, issue lists at 50, and cycle detection is iterative so a 50,000-node graph does not overflow the stack (tested). `ci.yml`, `build.yml` and `security.yml` gained concurrency groups - without them two pushes a minute apart ran everything twice, including twelve browser checks.

## Accessibility effect

`impactSummary` is the text equivalent of the canvas highlight, and it states plainly when Arq has no drawn preview rather than showing nothing. Every disabled action carries a reason; the type has no shape for a disabled control without one. Separately, the status bar is no longer a live region (above), and the file-open surface now says "compatible" and "may not be complete" as the separate facts the governed file-flow policy requires them to be.

## Project format and migration effect

None from the MCP boundary. `fileImpact.nativeSchemaChange` on the architecture profile is `false` and `migrationRequired` is `false`, because nothing here touches a file. The declared `vehicle.concept` profile records that registering it *would* change the native schema and need a compatibility window - one of its seven blockers. The arqfs semantic hash is versioned to `arq.semantic-hash.v2` rather than changed in place.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. Zero new runtime or dev dependencies; `pnpm-lock.yaml` changes only to add the workspace package. `check:dependency-licences` passes.

## Security and privacy effect

This is the substance of the change.

- Every bridge method takes a `GrantContext` first: subject, tenant, client, scopes, exact projects, expiry, revocation, checked on every call. An unwired application gets a server where every tool answers "nothing is shared with this connection".
- A project outside the grant and one that does not exist give the same error, so one grant cannot enumerate an operator's other projects.
- Commit lives on `ArqOperatorSurface`, an object the server is never constructed with. The guarantee is scope, not a flag.
- Provenance is derived from the `initialize` handshake and the server clock. `rightsStatus: "user_attests_permitted"` is not in the input vocabulary - software does not attest to a person's reuse rights.
- Reference URIs are parsed: no credentials, no IP literals, no reserved namespaces, no non-default ports, ASCII only. Nothing is ever fetched.
- The audit trail stores a request fingerprint and never request content, so it can prove what happened without becoming a second copy of every plan.
- The loopback HTTP endpoint requires a pairing token compared in constant time, refuses `localhost` (whose resolution can be redirected), and refuses every request when unpaired.
- `check-secrets.mjs` had no tests, so a regex broken by an edit would have reported a clean tree for ever. Its patterns are now pinned by `check-secrets-test.mjs`, which runs before the scan in CI.

## Rollback

Delete the package and remove it from the workspace; nothing in the product imports it. The fixes outside `packages/mcp-server` are independent commits and revert individually. Once the application bridge exists, rollback becomes: revoke grants, disable the server, leave committed revisions untouched. Staged proposals are not project history.

Bumps the minor-and-patch group with 2 updates in the / directory: [playwright](https://github.com/microsoft/playwright) and [turbo](https://github.com/vercel/turborepo). Updates `playwright` from 1.61.1 to 1.62.0
Release notes

Sourced from playwright's releases.

v1.62.0

🧱 New component testing model

Component testing moves to a stories and galleries model. A story wraps your component in one specific scenario — hard-coded props, mock data, providers — and a gallery page that you serve renders stories on demand. The new fixtures.mount() fixture navigates to the gallery, mounts a story by id, and returns a Locator scoped to the story's root element:

test('click should expand', async ({ mount }) => {
  const component = await mount('components/Expandable/Stateful');
  await component.getByRole('button').click();
  await expect(component.getByTestId('expanded')).toHaveValue('true');
});

Pass a story type as a template argument to type-check its props, and use update(props) / unmount() on the returned locator to re-render or tear down within a test.

🛑 Cancel operations with AbortSignal

Most operations and web-first assertions now accept a signal option that takes an AbortSignal, letting you cancel long-running actions, navigations, waits, and assertions:

const controller = new AbortController();
setTimeout(() => controller.abort(), 1000);

await page.getByRole('button', { name: 'Submit' }).click({ signal: controller.signal });

await expect(page.getByText('Done')).toBeVisible({ signal: controller.signal });

Providing a signal does not disable the default timeout; pass timeout: 0 to disable it.

🖼️ WebP screenshots

expect(page).toHaveScreenshot() and expect(locator).toHaveScreenshot() can now store snapshots in the WebP format — just give the snapshot a .webp name:

// Visual comparisons store the golden snapshot as lossless WebP.
await expect(page).toHaveScreenshot('homepage.webp');

// Standalone screenshots can trade quality for size with lossy WebP.

await page.screenshot({ path: 'homepage.webp', quality: 50 });

page.screenshot() and [locator.screenshot() (https://playwright.dev/docs/api/class-locator#locator-screenshot) also accept webp as a type, where quality 100 (the default) is lossless and lower values use lossy compression.

🧩 Custom test filtering with Reporter.preprocess()

New reporter.preprocess() hook runs after the configuration is resolved and before reporter.onBegin(), letting a reporter mark individual tests as skipped, excluded, fixed, or failing through a TestRun object:

title: Bump actions/download-artifact from 4 to 8
body:
Bumps [actions/download-artifact](https://github.com/actions/download-artifact) from 4 to 8.
Release notes

Sourced from actions/download-artifact's releases.

v8.0.0

v8 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v8 has been migrated to an ESM module. This should be transparent to the caller but forks might need to make significant changes.

[!IMPORTANT] Hash mismatches will now error by default. Users can override this behavior with a setting change (see below).

Direct downloads

To support direct uploads in actions/upload-artifact, the action will no longer attempt to unzip all downloaded files. Instead, the action checks the Content-Type header ahead of unzipping and skips non-zipped files. Callers wishing to download a zipped file as-is can also set the new skip-decompress parameter to true.

Enforced checks (breaking)

A previous release introduced digest checks on the download. If a download hash didn't match the expected hash from the server, the action would log a warning. Callers can now configure the behavior on mismatch with the digest-mismatch parameter. To be secure by default, we are now defaulting the behavior to error which will fail the workflow run.

ESM

To support new versions of the @actions/* packages, we've upgraded the package to ESM.

What's Changed

  • Don't attempt to un-zip non-zipped downloads by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#460
  • Add a setting to specify what to do on hash mismatch and default it to error by @​danwkennedy in actions/download-artifact#461

Full Changelog: https://github.com/actions/download-artifact/compare/v7...v8.0.0

v7.0.0

v7 - What's new

[!IMPORTANT] actions/download-artifact@v7 now runs on Node.js 24 (runs.using: node24) and requires a minimum Actions Runner version of 2.327.1. If you are using self-hosted runners, ensure they are updated before upgrading.

Node.js 24

This release updates the runtime to Node.js 24. v6 had preliminary support for Node 24, however this action was by default still running on Node.js 20. Now this action by default will run on Node.js 24.

What's Changed

title: Zeus 5.0: boundary-safe routing, blast radius, method selection and typed evidence
body:
Upgrades the Arq operating system from Zeus 4.0 to 5.0. The uploaded `ZEUS_ARQ_OPERATOR_OS_2.0` package was used as reference material and critiqued, not installed as an overlay.

## Problem

Zeus 4 was fast and deterministic where it counted, but three things were wrong, and all three are reproducible on the Zeus 4 code:

**1. Trigger matching was a bare substring test.**

| Prompt | Zeus 4 routed | Through |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `explain how the build works` | `ui-visual` | "ui" inside "b**ui**ld" |
| `improve the wallpaper documentation typo` | `geometry` | "wall" inside "**wall**paper" |
| `rename a variable in the parser guide` | `ui-visual` | "ui" inside "g**ui**de" |

**2. Mode came from keyword presence, not the speech act.** `explain how the build works` classified as `implement` because it contains "build". Worse, the delivery stop was raised unconditionally whenever "deploy", "production" or "ship" appeared anywhere, so `explain the release process` compiled a contract whose stop was `production-verified`. A question about releasing was gated as a production deployment.

**3. Risk was the only gating axis.** A low-risk edit to `packages/arqfs` and a low-risk edit to a README were treated identically. Risk says how likely a change is to be wrong. It says nothing about how far a wrong version reaches or what undoing it costs.

Separately, `scripts/test-zeus-system.sh` could not pass on the base branch: the four lint fixture directories it depends on (`quality/architecture-clean|bad`, `quality/fixtures/security-clean|bad`) were never committed.

## Solution

**Routing.** Task and trigger are normalised the same way and matched on token and phrase boundaries with a bounded inflection suffix, so "walls" matches "wall" and "wallpaper" does not. Negative phrases added: "unit test" no longer routes geometry through "unit".

**Modes.** Read from clause openings. `answer` and `plan` modes cannot escalate the delivery stop, inherit the topic's risk, or buy a deep budget. Incidents are detected as a shared surface plus a failure word, so "the ci is failing on main" is caught where the fixed phrase "ci failing" was not.

**Two new axes.** Blast radius (`local`, `package`, `product`, `persistent`, `public`, `production`) and reversibility (`reversible`, `compensable`, `irreversible`), in `.zeus/blast-radius.json`. Derived from task language and, in `zeus impact`, from real changed paths, worst of the two winning. Either can raise a tier and add acceptance criteria; neither can lower anything. Persistent radius adds original-preserved, copy-on-write and recovery evidence; irreversible adds an operator confirmation step.

Building this surfaced an over-escalation defect of my own: a module matching on one weak token dragged `rename a variable in the parser guide` into a deep public lane. Weak matches now contribute a capped radius, and that case classifies as package/fast.

**Method selection.** New. `.zeus/method-registry.json` holds 98 retained methods (94 distinct behaviours, 4 aliases) with scopes, so selection is deterministic and scope-gated: a marketing method is never proposed for a geometry defect. `zeus method` prints the stack with the reason for each entry.

**Typed evidence.** Zeus 4 graded a run; Zeus 5 grades each claim (`verified`, `partially-verified`, `inferred`, `assumed`, `blocked`, `not-inspected`, `failed`). Only `verified` is green and it requires a command and exit code. A cached entry for a protected gate is downgraded automatically. `zeus evidence report` exits non-zero otherwise.

**One invariant register.** `.zeus/INVARIANTS.md`, 85 invariants in 13 sections, replacing copies that had drifted between the kernel and the modules. Modules apply it, reviewer agents verify against it, neither restates it.

**Independent reviewers.** Six domain reviewer subagents plus an orchestrator under `.claude/agents/`, each bound to the invariant sections it verifies and named by the compiled contract.

**Self-validation.** `zeus validate` cross-checks manifests, registries, skills, agents, hooks and schemas against each other. It fails if the Arq language guardian is ever removed from the hook chain, or if a Zeus skill stops pointing at a `.zeus/` source.

### Deliberately not adopted from the reference package

- Its `.claude/rules/` and `docs/operator-source/` trees duplicated `.zeus/modules/`, `docs/adr/` and `STATUS.md`. Installing them would have created a second source of truth for the same invariants. Content folded into `.zeus/INVARIANTS.md` instead.
- Its blocking write-time language guard duplicated the Arq Language System 4.1 (em dashes, hype, prohibited claims, interoperability overclaims) using path heuristics instead of real scope resolution, and blocked at write time where this repository deliberately warns at write and blocks in CI. Reduced to the product-safety absolutes the Language System does not carry, made warn-only, and scoped to files outside the guardian's reach so the two never double-report.
- Its 38 granular skills were kept but rewritten as thin routers into `.zeus/`, so a skill cannot drift from the module it describes.
- Its guards matched destructive patterns against the whole serialised tool payload, which blocks writing documentation that quotes a rejected pattern. Rewritten to match commands against commands and paths against paths.

## Non-goals

- No change to Engineering OS 5.0, which remains the merge authority, or to the Arq Language System 4.1, which remains the language authority.
- No product code touched. This is operating-system and tooling only.
- `scripts/zeus-architecture-lint.mjs` still cannot tell a sentence stating a prohibition from one breaching it. Documented as a known limitation in the clean fixture rather than fixed here.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable. No user-facing surface changes.

## Tests

New, all passing:

- `scripts/zeus-classification-test.mjs`, 14 cases over `quality/fixtures/zeus-classification-cases.json`. Every routing and mode defect above is pinned, plus the new axes and scope gating.
- `scripts/zeus-guard-test.mjs`, 13 cases over `quality/fixtures/zeus-guard-cases.json`, pinning both sides of the guard: what must be blocked, and what must not (documenting a rejected pattern, editing an ArqScript `.arq` source, editing the env template, `grep process.env`).
- `scripts/zeus-validate.mjs`, OS consistency.
- Evidence-ledger assertion in the system test: a run containing a `not-inspected` claim must not grade green.
- The four missing lint fixture directories, so `scripts/test-zeus-system.sh` passes end to end for the first time.

Repository gates, all run locally at this head:

```
bash scripts/test-zeus-system.sh    Zeus 5 full system tests passed.
pnpm format:check                   All matched files use Prettier code style
pnpm lint                           clean
pnpm typecheck                      36/36 successful
pnpm test                           244 files, 2038 tests passed
pnpm arq:language:verify            passed
pnpm arq:language:audit:ci          93 files scanned, no hard violations, Gate PASS
pnpm engineering:context:verify     ok: true
pnpm engineering:policy             internally consistent
pnpm engineering:bindings           66 paths checked, no warnings
```

### CI corrections after the first push

Three checks failed on the first commit and were fixed in `fb91e6d`:

- **`preflight`**: the generated engineering context was stale. This change moves files inside the context's hashed source set, so it had to be rebuilt in the same commit, the same rule the Language System applies to its own context.
- **`engineering-gate`**: a cascade, not a separate defect. It downloads the selected-evidence artifact that `preflight` never produced.
- **`lint-and-typecheck`**: `format:check` failed on the three hook files and one skill. My first local run resolved Prettier through `npx` before `node_modules` existed, so it reported a different file set than the pinned version. Re-run with the pinned Prettier and fixed. The claim in an earlier revision of this description that 29 files were already unformatted on the base branch was wrong and came from that same bad run; the base branch is clean.

## Performance effect

Improved. `node scripts/zeus-benchmark.mjs --iterations 500` reports `status: green` with compile+route p95 at **0.49 ms** against a 5 ms target, and the fast contract at **972 chars** against a 4000 char budget despite the added fields. Trigger regexes are compiled once at module load rather than per call. Index cache hit 237 ms (target 250), context query 113 ms (target 500).

## Accessibility effect

None directly. The `arq-ux-accessibility-reviewer` agent now encodes the accessibility invariants (44 by 44 CSS pixel targets, no hover-only action, status never carried by colour alone) so they are checked by an addressable reviewer rather than by convention.

## Project format and migration effect

None. No `.arq` schema, migration or persistence code is touched. The change makes `.arq` work *harder* to get wrong: `packages/arqfs`, `packages/project-format`, `packages/local-storage`, `**/migrations/**` and `database/**` now classify as `persistent` blast radius, which forces the deep tier and adds original-preserved, copy-on-write-verified and recovery-exercised acceptance criteria.

One repository-specific correction worth noting: `.arq` is also the ArqScript source extension here (`examples/arqscript/basic-house.arq` is ASCII text). The guard checks for the SQLite magic header, so real containers are protected while ArqScript sources stay editable.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No dependency added, removed or upgraded. All new code is Node built-ins only.

## Security and privacy effect

Net improvement, with one deliberate trade-off.

Added: a `PreToolUse` guard blocking destructive commands, secret and env-file access, edits to real project containers, and off-box transfer of project databases; a deny list for `.env`, secrets, credentials, private keys and `.pem` files; a `Stop` guard blocking a completion claim made with no tool evidence at all.

Trade-off: a Bash command that merely *quotes* `rm -rf /` or `.env` is blocked, because that cannot be distinguished from executing it without parsing the shell. This is intentional and conservative. It caught two of my own commands during development, both rephrased. Path- and content-based false positives are fixed: the guard no longer inspects the whole serialised payload.

No secret material added. The security lint fixture uses SQLite pragmas rather than credential-shaped strings so it cannot trip secret scanning.

## Rollback

Revert the two commits. Nothing outside the repository is touched: no migration, no deployment, no published artifact, no external state. The pre-Zeus-5 system is restored intact by the revert, though `engineering:context:build` should be re-run afterwards so the generated context matches the reverted sources.

The one behaviour to expect on revert is that `scripts/test-zeus-system.sh` returns to failing on the missing lint fixtures, as it does on the base branch today.

title: Proof-gap closures, 3D conflict resolution, and ARQ Interaction Foundation 1.0 (wall Context HUD)
body:
## Problem

Three bodies of work, all driven to verified completion: (1) the Engineering OS's recorded proof gaps (`browser_journal_recovery`, `browser_model_canvas`) and the 3D status conflict; (2) the ARQ Interaction Foundation 1.0 package — a Context HUD in the real wall workflow with motion, positioning, feedback, and input-ownership primitives; (3) gate defects the new evidence surfaced (unmapped command ids, missing Chromium install, evidence self-pollution).

## Solution

**Proof-gap closures + 3D resolution** (commits `536f919`…): journal-recovery and model-canvas capability checks close both browser proof gaps; the 3D check's reachability + WebGL2 + bidirectional shared-selection evidence resolves `CONFLICT-3D-CURRENT-STATUS` through its documented path — STATUS.md, both conflict registries, the claim registry (`3d-current` → CURRENT), public bindings, product copy, the marketing conflict-gate test, and the model-canvas contract updated together with a logged language refresh. The OS gained the `RESOLVED` conflict status its vocabulary lacked.

**Interaction Foundation 1.0** (`52ee878`, `4700bda`): adapted into `packages/design-system/src/interaction-foundation/` —
- *Motion*: token vocabulary (`instant/micro/fast/normal/deliberate`, `fast=120ms` promoting the shipped literal) as CSS custom properties + TS mirror; damped spring profiles; reduced-motion hook; the five hardcoded transition literals and three duplicated menu shadows tokenised.
- *Overlays*: `ContextHud` — Floating UI (`offset+flip+shift`) over a **ref-anchored stable virtual element** with imperative reposition (zero React renders per pointer move), positioning and Motion presence on separate elements, `--arq-z-context-hud: 90` in the documented tier policy, pointer-transparent surface (interactive children opt back in).
- *Feedback*: W135 ToastRegion — pure capped/grouping/pausable store (+7 tests) and an `aria-live` region at `--arq-z-toast`; replaces App's broken ad-hoc notice (z-index 9, three phantom tokens). Wall commits, validation failures, deletes, undo/redo all flow through it.
- *Input ownership*: shared `isEditableEventTarget`/`shouldRouteShortcutToEditor`, deduplicating both inline copies; Ctrl/Cmd+Z / +Shift+Z undo-redo finally implemented per the registry.
- *Wall pilot*: typing digits during preview auto-focuses the HUD field; text lives in the tool's own `numeric-overlay` (extended with `setFieldText`; distance parsing now delegates to the existing `parseMetricLength`, so `3.5m` → 3500 mm — one parser); Enter places through the identical `placePoint` path a click uses; empty-Enter/double-click/Escape keep existing semantics; snapped points stay bit-exact when no override is typed.
- *Boundaries*: rule-driven `check:editor-dependency-boundaries` over `quality/editor-dependency-boundaries.json` (Lenis, Radix, Zustand, GSAP, R3F/Drei, React Flow, Animate UI — imports and manifest declarations), in CI and the evidence catalog.
- *Dependencies added*: `motion`, `@floating-ui/react` (licence-clean). TanStack Virtual deliberately not added — the one large list is served by the repo-owned model-panel virtualiser. React Aria untouched as the accessibility foundation.

**Three interaction defects found by building the browser proof, all fixed**: handlers read the one-frame-stale `draftPoints` mirror (now the tool's own points); Escape's pop tiers parked the lifecycle where `placePoint` refuses, silently swallowing the next click (pre-existing; now re-enters preview); the HUD surface swallowed the pointer moves it anchored beside (the register's "HUD blocking the active snap target" failure; now pointer-transparent).

**Gate fixes** (`715c635`): three catalog ids had no approved command mapping; the gate job never installed Chromium; `verify-policy` now proves every available command has a mapping at policy time.

## Non-goals

`e2e_arq_open` / `e2e_import_export` (product pipeline work, recorded with closure criteria); protected `arq-critical-change` environment reviewers, branch protection, merge queue (owner repo-settings actions); no renderer rewrite, no state-architecture change, no Lenis anywhere in the product.

## Visual evidence

`benchmarks/results/model-canvas-visual-*.png` (3D surface with shared-selection highlight); wall-HUD assertion records in `benchmarks/results/wall-hud-capability-*.json`.

## Tests

Wall-HUD check: 19 assertion groups, 3 consecutive green runs. Journal-recovery and model-canvas checks: 3 consecutive green runs each. 2055 unit tests (17 new: feedback store, motion tokens, numeric-overlay `setFieldText`/metric parsing). Engineering fixtures (16 classifier + 7 evidence + downgrade guard), policy, context, strict bindings `ready`; all language gates including hard audit and rendered-site proof; format, lint, typecheck green.

## Performance effect

Render-frame: 21.5 ms first frame vs 2000 ms budget. Workspace-layout: 8/8 viewports. Dialog and hover-sequence checks green. HUD anchoring adds zero React renders per pointer move by design; feedback queue hard-capped.

## Accessibility effect

HUD field has accessible name/description, `aria-invalid` + text error (colour never sole indicator); feedback region `aria-live="polite"`, never steals focus; keyboard-only wall entry proven end to end; reduced-motion flow proven functional; focus handed back to the workspace on HUD close.

## Project format and migration effect

None — journal behavior proven unchanged by the journal-recovery check; no `.arq` format changes.

## Dependency and licence effect

`motion` + `@floating-ui/react` added to `@arq/design-system`; SBOM regenerated, all 287 packages within policy; lockfile regenerated by pnpm.

## Security and privacy effect

Editor dependency boundaries enforced in CI and gate evidence; no new network access; overlay layers follow the documented z-tier policy.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. All additions are additive modules, checks, and registry states; reverting restores prior behavior verbatim. No data migration.

title: Z Voice: mechanical update-and-log loop for every governed change
body:
## Problem

The Z Voice gates catch a stale context, but the record of *what changed and when* was manual. A change to governed sources could refresh the context without leaving any log of which source sets moved, and AI-written docs prose got no write-time check (only the CI audit).

## Solution

**Every substantive change logs itself, enforced.**

- `refresh-arq-language-context.mjs`: when the source-set digest changes, appends an entry to `docs/product/voice/context/REFRESH-LOG.json` with the new digest, the previous digest and the exact source sets that moved. Re-running with no change appends nothing.
- `verify-arq-language-context.mjs` (the CI freshness gate): fails if the log is missing, has no entries, does not record changed source sets, or does not carry the committed context's digest. An update to governed sources therefore cannot merge unlogged.
- The log lives under `docs/product/voice/context/`, which is not a hashed source set, so writing it cannot invalidate the context it describes.

**AI-written prose checked at write time.** The warn-only guardian hook now also covers `docs/pages`, `docs/product`, `docs/ai` and `docs/interoperability` — the same bases the hard audit scans — excluding `docs/product/voice`, whose audit records quote violations on purpose and are governed by the acknowledgement contract. `arq:language:audit:ci` remains the blocking gate, unchanged.

**Standing instruction.** `CLAUDE.md` now states the loop for every future session: touch a governed source, run `pnpm arq:language:refresh` once in the same change, run the ladder before pushing, never bypass a guardian warning. The voice changelog records this release.

## Evidence

Enforcement proven in a scratch checkout with the real scripts:

- deleted log → `FAIL context refresh log missing`
- STATUS.md changed without refresh → freshness FAIL (2 failures: stale + unlogged)
- one refresh → PASS, latest log entry records `changedSourceSets: ["status"]`
- log entry digest tampered → `FAIL context change is not logged`

Guardian probe in `docs/product/` containing an AI-artifact marker and an AI professional-authority claim raised both hard findings; a file inside `docs/product/voice/` stays exempt.

Green locally at this head: the full language ladder including the new log gate, `site:build:verify` over 18 routes, `pnpm test` (244 files, 2038 tests), lint, typecheck, `format:check`, build.

## Rollback

Revert the commit. The log file and the two script changes are additive; the guardian scope change is warn-only.

title: Install Engineering OS 5.0: deterministic gate, registries, and repo alignment fixes
body:
## Problem

The ARQ Engineering OS 5.0 package (uploaded as `ARQ_ENGINEERING_OS_5.0.zip`) was audited against this repository but not installed: no deterministic change classification, no evidence gate, a CI push trigger pointing at the nonexistent `main` branch, no `merge_group` coverage, `@REPLACE` CODEOWNERS placeholders, and a dead `/packages/security/` ownership rule. The package itself contained defects that would have broken or neutered the installed system, and while this PR was in review the base branch landed Arq Language System 4.1 (#283) and its update-and-log loop (#285), which resolved the OS's biggest recorded blocker and had to be interlocked.

## Solution

Installs the package under `engineering/` per `ops/installation-map.v5.json` and drives it to a fully green gate:

- `engineering/ops` registries, verifier tools, fixtures, audit docs, docs 30–35, record templates; five `engineering:*` package scripts.
- `.github/workflows/engineering-gate.yml` in **shadow mode**: classify diff → preflight verifiers → selected evidence → protected-approval semantics → final gate. **Green end to end on this PR.**
- `ci.yml` push covers the real default branch and declares `merge_group`; CODEOWNERS names the repository owner across product-truth, geometry, security, control-plane, and L4 ingress/persistence surfaces.
- **LS 4.1 interlock** (after #283/#285 merged): `language_contract` and `rendered_public_site` evidence flipped to `available` and pass in the gate; `deployed_public_site` is recorded as enforced by deploy-pages' `verify-live-language` job; bindings report `ready` with zero warnings; the language-context refresh is logged per the #285 loop.

Defects found and fixed along the way, each locked by a fixture or proven in CI:

1. Package: `33_IMPLEMENTATION_HANDOFF.md` was a declared context source but missing from the installation map (context build failed).
2. Package: control-plane globs referenced a pre-install layout, so the gate could not protect itself (fixture 12); evidence-catalog commands pointed at the same dead layout.
3. Package: the reference workflow uploaded dot-prefixed artifacts, which `upload-artifact@v4` silently excludes — every classify run failed.
4. Package: the bindings verifier required HEAD to equal the audited commit, failing every PR branch by construction; now ancestor semantics with a distinct shallow-clone message, plus `fetch-depth: 0` where it runs as evidence.
5. Package: the gate polluted its own `format` evidence by downloading artifacts into the checked workspace; gate runtime records are now prettier/git-ignored.
6. Repo: `api/**` (OpenAPI contract), `database/**` (server schema), `**/Cargo.lock`, `scripts/zeus.mjs`, `scripts/lib/**`, `.claude/**`, and the evidence-defining configs (`vitest.config.ts`, `eslint.config.mjs`, `turbo.json`, `tsconfig.base.json`, `.prettierignore`) were unmapped or under-classified; all now classify correctly (fixtures 13–16).
7. Repo: `scripts/run-design-system-dialog-capability-check.mjs` raced React Aria's unmount-time focus restore (~1 in 4 CI failures); both focus assertions now poll with a 2 s ceiling, with committed result records of the reproduction and fix.
8. Docs/registries recording LS 4.1 as absent were updated to the merged reality; the conflict registry's 3D entry now quotes STATUS.md's actual DISPUTED wording. CLAUDE.md carries the Zeus-is-advisory note doc 30 required.

## Non-goals

- Repo-settings actions reserved to the owner: protected `arq-critical-change` environment reviewers, branch protection / required checks, merge queue (Phase 3 of `engineering/33_IMPLEMENTATION_HANDOFF.md`).
- Closing recorded proof gaps (`browser_journal_recovery`, `e2e_arq_open`, `browser_model_canvas`, `e2e_import_export`), the 3D status conflict, or assigning the nine `UNASSIGNED` contract owners — deliberate owner decisions, recorded not guessed.

## Visual evidence

Not applicable — no user-facing UI changes.

## Tests

All 13 checks green on the PR head, including the full Engineering Gate chain. Locally: 16 classifier + 7 evidence fixtures + downgrade guard; policy, engineering-context, and strict bindings (`ready`, zero warnings); all 13 `arq:language` checks plus rendered-site proof; format, lint, typecheck, 2038 unit tests. Self-test: this PR's own diff classifies L4 control-plane, manual review required, zero unknown files; a skipped protected approval yields `needs_review`, an approval yields `pass`.

## Performance effect

None at runtime. One shadow-mode workflow per PR; preflight verifiers run in seconds.

## Accessibility effect

None (the dialog capability-check fix changes assertion timing, not product behavior).

## Project format and migration effect

None — no `.arq` format, persistence, or migration code is touched.

## Dependency and licence effect

None — no dependencies added or changed; engineering tools use only Node built-ins.

## Security and privacy effect

Strengthens control-plane protection: CI workflows, CODEOWNERS, the engineering system, Zeus's engine, agent-hook wiring, and the configs that define lint/test/build/format evidence all classify L4 with protected-approval evidence; the server API contract and database schema classify with the collaboration/auth surface. No secrets, no new network access.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. The engineering system is additive; reverting restores the prior CI triggers, CODEOWNERS, and check script verbatim. No data or format migration to unwind.

title: Arq Language System 4.1 (Z Voice): one governed vocabulary, gated claims, deployed-site proof
body:
## Problem

The public site said things the repository could not support, and nothing checked it.

- The deployed site carried 132 rendered U+2014 em dashes across its 18 routes.
- `/` said an `.arq` file "opens in your browser" while `FileOpenPanel` stops at a compatibility verdict and the OPFS worker is never constructed.
- `/` also collapsed the IndexedDB demo journal into "saving is a local write" on a `.arq` file, which are two different persistence tiers.
- `/interoperability` said "every import in Arq produces an import report" while no import path is reachable from the product.
- `/security` said the build "sends nothing anywhere" with no network-observation evidence.
- `/students` said "a modest laptop is enough" with no published hardware profile.
- `/pricing` and `/status` gave lifetime guarantees ("can never lock you out", "our outage can never be your outage") that no commercial or architectural decision backs.
- `/product` published "175 tests" and an affirmative "full IFC authoring" with no negation in the sentence.
- `STATUS.md` asserted both a wired 3D tab and a 3D stack with zero consumers, so any surface could quote whichever half suited it.
- CI checked TypeScript source only. A source-only pass could coexist with a stale or non-compliant deployed site.

## Solution

Install Arq Language System 4.1, named Z Voice, as a versioned, source-owned, machine-checkable layer, then bring the copy in line with it.

**Truth before wording.** Nine conflicts are active in `docs/product/voice/conflict-registry.json` and block their claims from public, support, documentation and product-AI surfaces. Two are deliberately left unresolved because they cannot be settled from inside this change:

- `CONFLICT-3D-CURRENT-STATUS`. `ModelCanvas.tsx` exists and `App.tsx` renders it for a `3d` tab, but no test covers that surface and no headless-browser check exercises it, so there is no reachability evidence of the kind the wall-drawing, OPFS and file-open claims have. `STATUS.md` now records the dispute instead of asserting either side, and no public page states 3D as available or as absent.
- `DECISION-PERSISTENCE-TIERS`. ADR-0019/0024 commit to SQLite-WASM over OPFS while `packages/local-storage` ships a tested Dexie/IndexedDB implementation. That needs an ADR from the architecture owner. Until it exists, no surface may describe a journal write as a portable `.arq` write.

**Public copy.** Every em dash removed by rewriting the sentence, not substituting the character: full stops, colons, parentheses, restructuring. `docs/product/voice/PUBLIC-COPY-REMEDIATION-4.1.md` drove the rest, page by page. `/interoperability` now uses Arq's eight fidelity results (Preserved, Converted, Approximated, Flattened, Omitted, Unsupported, Retained as opaque data, Failed). Each changelog entry cites the repository paths or checks behind it. The self-attesting register ("honest", "genuinely", "will not pretend") is gone: the pages state the source, the behaviour or the limit instead.

**Product UI.** `describeSaveState` names the persistence tier ("Saved locally", "Saving locally...", "Recovered locally") because a bare "Saved" read as a portable `.arq` write. `formatCoordinates` returns "Off canvas" rather than a lone dash, matching its sibling "No snap" / "No selection". `state-language-map.json` gains the `web-plan-journal-status` machine so every visible save state reaches a canonical message.

**Machinery.** 21 checks under `scripts/`, 18 pnpm scripts, canonical data under `docs/product/voice/`. The generated context is hashed from the 29 source sets in `context-contract.json`.

**CI and deployment.** A `language-system` job runs the checks in the documented order and never regenerates the committed context: a stale context must fail and be refreshed by the change that moved its sources. The Pages workflow verifies route coverage before the build, audits the rendered output, writes a commit-bound proof with a sha256 per route into the artifact, exposes `page_url`, and runs a post-deployment job that reads the proof and every route back off the published URL and requires the exact SHA (8 attempts, 5s apart).

## Z Voice verification (second commit)

The voice system is also recorded under its name Z Voice in `docs/product/voice/README.md` and `docs/product/VOICE-SYSTEM.md`. An exhaustive check of the integration archive against the repo: all 151 files accounted for (43 byte-identical, 60 differing only by Prettier formatting, 31 deliberate adaptations reviewed diff by diff, 0 missing); the CI fragment's commands match the `language-system` job exactly; every gate in the Pages fragment is present, plus direct verifier invocations the fragment did not require; 20 of 20 fragment pnpm scripts, 6 of 6 claim-gate tests, the guardian hook and the package manifest are all consumed or recorded; every repo path cited by the registries exists. Eleven scripts kept package-layout bare-invocation defaults that failed without flags; their defaults now resolve the repo layout and all 12 verifiers pass when run bare from the repository root, with wired invocations unchanged.

## Non-goals

- Resolving the 3D conflict. That needs a browser capability check for the 3D tab, not a copy edit.
- Deciding the persistence-tier ADR, publishing pricing, or writing legal terms and the privacy notice. Those need their owners.
- Building a runtime support bot or any AI feature. The answerability outcomes (ANSWER, QUALIFY, CONFLICT, UNKNOWN, REFUSE_AUTHORITY) ship as a tested, documented integration boundary with no consumer.
- Reformatting or rewording docs outside the language system's surfaces.

## Visual evidence

Headless-Chromium pass over all 17 public routes plus the 404, at desktop (1440) and 320px, on the built output served under `/Arq`: every route resolves, one `h1` each, no horizontal overflow, no external resource, no failed request, no U+2014 in rendered text.

Rendered em dash count by route, before and after:

| Route | Before | After |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| `/` | 8 | 0 |
| `/product` | 9 | 0 |
| `/architects` | 12 | 0 |
| `/students` | 9 | 0 |
| `/collaboration` | 5 | 0 |
| `/ai` | 11 | 0 |
| `/interoperability` | 7 | 0 |
| `/ipad` | 6 | 0 |
| `/pricing` | 6 | 0 |
| `/security` | 9 | 0 |
| `/docs` | 7 | 0 |
| `/changelog` | 12 | 0 |
| `/status` | 4 | 0 |
| `/contact` | 6 | 0 |
| `/legal/privacy` | 5 | 0 |
| `/legal/terms` | 5 | 0 |
| `/legal/open-source` | 5 | 0 |
| `/404` | 6 | 0 |
| **Total** | **132** | **0** |

Also verified: `pnpm benchmark:workspace-layout` passes at all 8 viewports with the longer save-state labels (result committed under `benchmarks/results/`).

## Tests

Green locally at the current head: `pnpm test` (244 files, 2038 tests), `pnpm lint`, `pnpm typecheck` (36 packages plus `contracts/`), `pnpm format:check`, `pnpm build`, `pnpm check:workspace-registries`, `pnpm check:dependency-licences`.

Language ladder, all passing: `arq:language:sources:verify`, `install:verify`, `public:verify`, `routes:verify`, `editorial:verify`, `context:verify`, `data:verify`, `state:verify`, `adapters:verify`, `conflicts:verify`, `claims:verify`, `verify`, `audit:ci`, `bundle:verify`, and `site:build:verify` against `apps/marketing/dist`.

The deployed-site verifier was exercised against a local server holding the built artifact: it passes on the correct commit and fails on a wrong one.

`pages.test.ts` gains the claim-gate suite: public current-state assertions must bind to a non-blocked claim record, each public binding must appear in the inventory, each rendered route must map to exactly one inventory entry, no page may render U+2014, release-ladder text must be labelled as scope, compatibility must not read as an opened project, and the 3D conflict must not be settled in either direction.

**Live GitHub Pages verification has not run on this branch.** The `github-pages` environment restricts deployments to the base branch, so `deploy` is refused here and `verify-live-language` is skipped. Merging this PR puts the change on the base branch, where the environment permits deployment and the live check runs.

## Performance effect

None expected. No runtime code path changed; the site is still static with no JavaScript required. The additions are build-time and CI-time checks.

## Accessibility effect

Small improvement. `formatCoordinates` now returns "Off canvas" instead of a bare em dash, which a screen reader announced as nothing. Save-state labels stay in the same `aria-live` region and remain plain words. The per-page landmark, skip-link, single-`h1` and focus assertions are unchanged and still pass.

## Project format and migration effect

None. No `.arq` schema, migration or recovery code changed. The change makes the language rules around those states stricter: a journal write may no longer be described as a portable-file write, and compatibility preflight may no longer be described as an opened project.

## Dependency and licence effect

None. No dependency added or removed. The licence gate and SBOM run unchanged, and `/legal/open-source` still renders from the generated SBOM.

## Security and privacy effect

Net positive. `/security` and `/legal/privacy` no longer make absolute transport claims the repository cannot evidence; they state the current architecture and name the missing network-observation test. The rendered and deployed verifiers fail the build if any public page loads a third-party script, style, image, font, frame or CSS `url()`, which turns the "no third-party resource" privacy statement into an enforced property rather than an assertion.

## Rollback

Revert the merge. Nothing is generated into the repository outside it, the pnpm scripts and CI jobs are additive, and the previous copy returns with the revert. To keep the language system but stop deploying from the in-flight branch, remove it from the `on.push.branches` list in `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml`.

title: Full-repo audit and completion: website, interactive canvas, validation, persistence, 3D view, real quality gates
body:
## Problem

A full-repository audit (8 parallel area audits) found the library layer strong and green but the product thin: the marketing website was 0 of 17 spec'd pages (`apps/marketing` was literally `export {}`), the canvas was a static painting, `@arq/validation` was an `export {}` stub, five data-layer libraries (including local-storage and the whole 3D stack) had zero consumers, the `ifc` format routed to an adapter id that did not exist, planning docs still described the repo as a spec-only ZIP, and several quality gates were fictional (`pnpm lint` ran zero tasks; three CI workflows were `echo` stubs).

## Solution

Ten commits, two rounds.

**Round 1 — foundations:**
1. **Public website** — all 17 PUB sheets from `docs/pages/` plus 404, static, no client JS, designed as an architectural drawing set; honesty enforced by tests (route coverage, landmarks, no external resources, launch-claims checklist as a failing test). Undecided facts (pricing/legal/status) publish the state of the decision, not placeholder fiction.
2. **Interactive canvas** — pan/zoom (wheel, pinch, space-drag), the ARQ-094 wall chain tool over the ARQ-045..052 snap pipeline with live glyphs, hit-test selection, fit; typed operations with real inverses on the undo stack.
3. **Docs truth pass** — new `STATUS.md`, backlog indexes regenerated to all 242 issues via a checked-in generator, ZIP-era root docs rewritten, ~12 READMEs corrected in both directions.
4. **Real quality gates** — eslint over the whole repo (first run caught a real bug), secret scan (1,810 files) in a real Security workflow, explicit Build workflow, honest weekly Benchmark workflow, `contracts/` typechecked. The new licence gate promptly caught eslint's `minimatch` Blue Oak licence — allow-listed through the policy's own process.

**Round 2 — completing the product loop:**
5. **`@arq/validation` implemented** (§4.3): wall-segment, unique-id and room-polygon rules with the product's error structure; consumed at the commit gate with plain-language notices; status-bar model-health counts computed from the real rules. Canvas state language completed per the monochrome rule (distinct line weight/dash per token, tests assert no state is indistinguishable); hover and marquee window/crossing selection with multi-select flowing through the shell.
6. **Real local persistence** — edits journal to IndexedDB via `@arq/local-storage` (ADR-0006 pattern) and recover on reload; save state reports the journal's true condition (`saved`/`saving`/`recovered`/`unsaved-changes`). Verified: draw, reload → recovered; delete, reload → persisted.
7. **3D view** — the workspace's 3D tab renders drawn walls as extruded solids (`geometry-3d` over `wallOutline`, 100 mm/2400 mm) in real WebGL via `@arq/model-renderer`, with orbit/pan/zoom/fit and raycast picking; selection is shared with the plan by construction (`applySharedSelection`).
8. **IFC bridged into the import pipeline** — `IfcIngressAdapter` (the `ifc-ingress` id `formats.ts` always routed to) wraps the real web-ifc reader, registered in the worker's default registry, honestly scoped to viewing/inspection with the policy size limit enforced before the WASM boundary.
9. **Critique passes** — five real defects found by driving the built app and adversarially reviewing my own additions, all fixed: wall tool dead after its first committed chain; double-click leaving a zero-length segment; undo leaving dangling selections (primary and secondary); pinch firing a phantom selection through a stale marquee; a non-brand colour in the 3D selection treatment.

## Non-goals

The `.arq` open-project pipeline (file-open → OPFS worker → workspace), export paths, sync backend/`apps/api`, and co-authoring remain open and are tracked honestly in `STATUS.md`.

## Visual evidence

Headless-Chromium runs against real builds at every step: website (1440/375/320 px, light+dark), wall drawing with snap glyphs, duplicate-wall warning notice with "1 warning" in the status bar, marquee multi-select → "Delete 2 walls", journal recovery across reloads ("Recovered · 2 operation(s) recovered"), and the 3D tab with orbit + click-to-select syncing to tree/inspector/context bar (SwiftShader WebGL).

## Tests

`pnpm test`: 243 files, **2,023 tests, all passing** (193 new this PR). `pnpm typecheck`: 36/36 packages + contracts. `pnpm lint`: real and green. `pnpm format:check`: clean.

## Performance effect

Site is static HTML with self-hosted latin-subset fonts (~140 KB). Canvases paint on state change only (no animation loops); 3D renders on demand and disposes geometry/materials on rebuild. Render benchmarks unchanged, now scheduled weekly in CI.

## Accessibility effect

Site pages: skip link, landmarks, single `h1`, reduced-motion, 320 px/200 % zoom, `prefers-color-scheme`. Workspace: validation notices use `role="status"`; both canvases have `aria-label`s; drawn-wall selection reuses `describeSelectedElementForAccessibility`; selection state is never colour-only (line treatments in 2D, opacity treatment in 3D).

## Project format and migration effect

No `.arq` schema changes. New: an IndexedDB operation journal (ADR-0006 pattern, `arq-local-db`) for the workspace document — append-only, replayed on boot, isolated per project id.

## Dependency and licence effect

Added dev-only at root: `eslint`, `typescript-eslint`. `apps/web` gains workspace deps (`validation`, `local-storage`, `model-renderer`, `geometry-3d`) plus `three@0.185` (already in the tree via model-renderer) and `fake-indexeddb` (dev). `BlueOak-1.0.0` added to the licence allow-list (policy doc + enforcing script together). Licence scan green; SBOM feeds the site's notices page.

## Security and privacy effect

Net positive: real secret scanning (PR + weekly); IFC bytes are size-gated before the WASM boundary with the worker as the documented kill switch; the site loads zero third-party resources and says so on its privacy page. All project data remains local.

## Rollback

Revert the commits in reverse order; each front is independently revertible. The IndexedDB journal database (`arq-local-db`) is regenerable user-local state — deleting it loses only demo-workspace edits. No migrations to unwind.
